# Melee — the build notes

**The archive. `CLAUDE.md` is the live rules; this is why each one exists.** It is not loaded
automatically — `grep -n` it for a symbol, a build number (`(m146`), or the words in his
report, and read the entry before touching that system. New notes go at the TOP of the
landmine list, in the same shape: what he said, what was actually wrong, what was measured.

## m824 -- ship_hall.glb: the mothership's belly hall and pod (T7a)

The hall was a BackSide open cylinder, two tori, a circle and a sphere around his eggs and glyphs (`ship_belly`). It is now one piece at the code's R 12.5 / H 6.5 / glassR 7.5, with the doorway gap at +X where nW leaves it. The pod rides the tether, so it is built in its group's frame like the diner saucer. Shipped unverified.

## m822 -- foot_dress.glb: the footbridge's foot on the beach (T6z)

m490 made the foot a place: a flagstone path, a works hut, a CLOSED board, a lifebuoy, a tideline and a bench. Each now has a piece at the code's spot and yaw. The board's face is one white material, so the code's red-while-closed / white-once-fixed switch becomes a tint, as with every other `_paint` piece. Shipped unverified.

## m820 -- footbridge.glb: the footbridge's span (T6y)

The footbridge's dock end was already dressed (pearl_dock, the bollards), but its span was still chords, posts and rotated BoxGeometry diagonals. The art is the code's own 2 m panel as a tile, both trusses and the deck together. Each `deck()` run gets n = round(L / 2) of them, which is exactly the code's panel count, so the posts land where the code's do. Shipped unverified.

## m816 -- shore_steps.glb: the cliff ladder pads and the ferry stair's treads (T6x)

A fresh scan of the builders shows the campaign is now mostly art. Of what is left: `buildSite` and `buildFarm` are his kits already (the count is high because their boxes stay as colliders), `buildBridge` is the m291 river and is skipped whenever the channel bridge is live, and `buildNeighbours` was checked before. This pass takes two small pieces that were still plain boxes. Shipped unverified.

## m814 -- gap_ramp.glb: the island gap ramp (T6w)

The in-run, the kicker arc and the landing are all point lists the code fits so a board clears the ground (m484). The art is one segment, given each pair's length and pitch, so the curve stays the code's and the walk quads stay the surface. The landing reuses the segment, widened. The site builder (`buildSite`) turned out to be his `site_kit` already, so it was skipped. Shipped unverified.

## m813 -- swing_span.glb: the swing bridge's moving span (T6v)

It is built in the group's own frame and parented under `O.grp`, so the existing swing turns it with no new code. The truss is the code's: nine verticals each side at k * half / 4, rising 3.2 + 2.6 (1 - |k| / 4) to the middle. Pairs with T6u's fixed parts. Shipped unverified.

## m811 -- swing_bridge.glb: the swing bridge's fixed parts (T6u)

The moving span is a group the code turns, and its barriers and warning lights animate, so they stay code. Everything that stands still is art: the two fixed spans as 1 m tiles, the piers and the pivot drum stretched to the river bed, the lamps and the red gate posts. Shipped unverified.

## m808 -- ferry_landing.glb: the ferry's landing stage (T6t)

The jetty runs to wherever the island's ground meets the water (`vEnd` is computed), so it is a tile. The piles reach the seabed, so they are stretched. The pontoon's float drums first showed through its deck: their tops were above deck level, so they now sit below it. Shipped unverified.

## m806 -- wf_barge.glb: the barge under crane 1 (T6s)

The cranes are already his. The barge they work over was the last piece of `wfCranes` still drawn as boxes. Same lesson as the crates: the deck plate first rendered black because it shared the hull's top face, and lifting it 2 cm fixed it. Shipped unverified.

## m802 -- island_exit.glb: the BASE-jump exit point (T6r)

The deck is the code's IBASE numbers: 3 wide and 9 long, 5 m of it over the edge. That puts the edge (dE) at local Y -.5 from the deck's centre, and the braces run from under the end down 4.35 m to land just behind it, as `pearlSeg` does. The way-on steps fit the ground, so they are one step piece placed per step. Shipped unverified.

## m798 -- metro_core.glb: the metro core's tower kit (T6q)

The metro core's towers are rolled at load: size, height and one of four palette materials. A fixed tower model would fit none of them. What every tower shares is a lobby, a roof tank, sometimes a roof unit, and the sky-bridges between them, so that is the art. The window bands stay code because each tower's band material is its own (m700: the grip dims one). Shipped unverified.

## m795 -- under_safe.glb: the crossways ladders and the safe house (T6p)

The last of the Underneath. The safe house is meant to be warm light at last after the tunnels (m524), so it is the one room in the kit with soft furnishings and crockery. The laid table's bowls sit at the code's own .7 + k * .55, staggered +-.25. Shipped unverified.

## m792 -- under_market.glb: the pump room, the hidden market, the camp (T6o)

The pump wheel sits at the code's own `U.pump.wheelAt` and is built static, ready to spin on X. The market's tarps are one white material, so the code's `tarp` / `tarp2` alternation carries over as a tint. With T6m to T6o, the Underneath's tunnels, cistern, dig, vault, pumps, market and camp all have art waiting. The crossways and safe house are left. Shipped unverified.

## m791 -- under_cistern.glb: the cistern's catwalks, the dig's cart and strongbox (T6n)

The catwalks are the code's 19.2 m span between the ledges, on legs down to the pit floor at y - 2.4. That is the depth the water drains to (m522), so the legs read as standing in the water when it is high and on dry stone when it is drained. Shipped unverified.

## m789 -- underneath.glb: the Underneath's tunnel tiles (T6m)

The tunnels are built by `run()` and `room()` at whatever length the plan asks, so this is a kit of one-metre tiles, not a map. The first preview baked a growth patch and a damp streak into every tile. Down a straight tunnel that read as a row of lit windows, a stripe per metre. Both came out: the growth is its own piece, to scatter. Anything in a tile repeats, so a tile should carry only what is really periodic (courses, joints, the pipe). Shipped unverified.

## m784 -- bunker_camp.glb: the rest of Merle's camp (T6l)

Six pieces at the code's spots. One thing caught on review: the mast's guys first ran to (cos a, -sin a). The code puts them at v = sin a * 3.5, and Blender +Y is +v, so it is +sin. Handedness again; check every angle written into a piece against the code's own u / v. Shipped unverified.

## m782 -- bunker.glb: Merle's bunker, container and inside (T6k)

The container's corrugation is the code's own rib pitch (.3), and the door leaves stand open at the code's +-.25 spots. Inside, the string wall is a fresh scatter of the same 16 clippings and 14 strings. It is NOT the code's `pins` positions: the code uses its own LCG and this uses Python's random, so the cork board's layout differs. The dirt mounds belong to the hill and stay code. Shipped unverified.

## m781 -- diner_saucer.glb: the replica saucer and its yard (T6j)

The saucer moves (m761: it can leave the yard), so its art is built in the group's own frame to be parented under `O.saucer`, not placed in the world. Its dome and green light stay code because they are animated. The yard's fence gets the code's missing corner post, at the gap's far side. Shipped unverified.

## m777 -- diner_site.glb: the sign tower and the UFO museum (T6i)

The museum's clippings were first put at the code's own u (R - .45). At 2 m up, that is outside a quonset whose wall is only 2.75 m off centre there, so they poked through the shell. They now sit at R - .95. Worth checking in the code too: its paper boxes have the same problem. Shipped unverified.

## m776 -- diner.glb: Saucer Joe's, shell and inside (T6h)

The diner was 51 boxes and open cylinders. It is now one shell and one interior, both at the code's origin and numbers, so they drop in with no transform. The round ends are smooth arcs, not the code's four facets, and the facets stay as colliders. The roof's round-end discs shared a top face with the slab and rendered as black wedges, so the discs now sit 5 mm inside. The neon frame and canvas signs stay code because they glow. Shipped unverified.

## m772 -- hollis_props.glb: the last of Camp Hollis (T6g)

The firing positions are one 0.8 m bag segment that the code places seven times per horseshoe, already yawed. The rest are single props at the code's spots. With T6d through T6g, every drawn box in `buildMilBase` has art waiting. Shipped unverified.

## m769 -- hollis_yard.glb: Camp Hollis's trucks, net, mast and cage (T6f)

The camo net is a 15 x 15 grid that sags with distance from the nearest of the code's four poles, with a two-tone patch pattern. The mast's guys run from 12 m out to the code's 6 m radius at its three angles. The beacon sphere stays code because it blinks. The cage's chain-link is double-sided ribbons, as on the factory fence. Shipped unverified.

## m768 -- hollis_camp.glb: Camp Hollis's watchtower and tents (T6e)

The watchtower's parapet is laid in staggered sandbag courses with no bevels: bevels took it from 1,400 faces to 4,100. The parapet is open at +Y, where the code's two short runs leave the ladder gap. I first put the command tent's fly on the wrong side. The code's fly is at v -2.7, which is 4.3 m toward +Y from the tent's centre at -7, so it faces the gate. Shipped unverified.

## m767 -- hollis_wall.glb: Camp Hollis's HESCO ring (T6d)

Camp Hollis (m745) was the largest builder with no art: 57 boxes. This covers its wall. A basket is a mesh cage, a liner bulging between the uprights and fill showing on top, tiled at the code's own 1.1 m cage pitch. The wire is real concertina coils turned along the run, not tori. As with the parts crates, the first render had black tops where the fill shared a face with the basket. The rest of the base (watchtower, tents, motor pool, mast, cage) is the next pass. Shipped unverified.

## m764 -- factory_walks.glb: the factory's rails, legs and stair treads (T6c)

The code's `rail()` draws a top bar, a knee bar and a post every 2 m. The art is that as a 2 m tile, plus a last post. The west-wall stair's 33 solid `grate` blocks get open treads with yellow nosings; the blocks stay as colliders. The preview's stair first climbed the wrong way; the piece itself puts the nosing on +Y, matching the code, whose steps climb toward -v. Shipped unverified.

## m760 -- factory_line.glb: arm pedestals, the chrome booth, the lift shaft (T6b)

Three more of the factory line's stand-ins. The arms' pedestals get a bolted base and a turntable. The chrome booth gets mirror-chrome sides, a glowing ceiling and strip curtains at both ends. The lift's four bare posts become a braced shaft, tiled a metre at a time to 13 m, with its platform face left open. Shipped unverified.

## m759 -- parts_stock.glb: the factory's crates of arms (T6a)

There is one piece per height the code uses (1.1 / 1.5 / 1.9 by k % 3), with the 1.1 one in steel, because the code paints it `c7` grey metal. In the first preview the crate tops and corner posts rendered black: they shared faces exactly with the slats under them. Nudging each apart by a few millimetres fixed it. Watch for this on any slatted piece. Shipped unverified.

## m755 -- control_room.glb: the factory control room's consoles and lever (T5z)

The three consoles were dark boxes with a green slab on top. They now have a raked desk with the line drawn on it (one panel amber) and three monitors. The lever is a red-knobbed handle on a hazard-collared pedestal. Its knob sits where the code's sphere was, so `leverAt` and the prompt are unchanged. Shipped unverified.

## m754 -- factory_stations.glb: the factory line's arches, cage, hats and boots (T5y)

The two arches are 4.2 and 3.4 tall, so each one is split into stretched posts and a fixed head. Scaling one piece would have squashed the head beam with it. The hard hats taken off the line's workers were cylinders; they are now domes with brims, tinted the code's yellow / white. The boots were plank boxes. Shipped unverified.

## m751 -- shed_vents.glb: the transit shed's roof vents (T5x)

The shed itself is his `wf_shed`, but the three 2.2 m `steel` boxes on its roof are drawn outside that branch, so they stayed boxes. Each is now a louvred vent with a hipped cap and a turbine ventilator, at the box's own size. Shipped unverified.

## m749 -- factory_skin.glb: the factory's parapet and green screens (T5w)

The parapet was four `panel` slabs and the screens were three flat `screen` boxes. Both are now one-metre tiles. The screen's bright dashes come from a seeded random per tile, so a run of tiles reads as text crawling along the wall rather than one stripe repeated. It does still repeat every metre if you look for it. The first preview faced the wrong way (+Y is OUT). Shipped unverified.

## m746 -- factory_gallery.glb: the gallery over the fence (T5v)

The gallery was a grate, two tin slabs and a roof slab. It is now a one-metre bay, tiled: corrugated walls, a window ribbon lit faintly green like the factory's screens, and a portal frame every metre. It is tiled so the corrugation and mullions keep their pitch. The code's slabs stay the colliders. Shipped unverified.

## m744 -- shed_yard.glb: the transit shed's pallets and drums (T5u)

The existing pallet (`ce_pallet`) is leaned on its end and the existing drums (`pp_drums`) come as a pair, so neither fits the shed's one-pallet-per-.15 stacks or its five single drums. These are a flat pallet to stack and one drum with a tintable body, so the code's c1 / c5 colours carry over. The lid is painted with the body, not left dark. Shipped unverified.

## m741 -- factory_portal.glb: the factory's intake door (T5t)

The code striped the door with alternating yellow and black blocks. The art uses true 45-degree chevrons: each band is a parallelogram clipped to its jamb or lintel. The first version only kept bands that crossed the whole rectangle, which left the 0.5 m jambs plain yellow, so the clip is now Sutherland-Hodgman. The pieces it replaces were all drawing-only, so nothing about collision moves. Shipped unverified.

## m737 -- factory_roof.glb: the factory's roof units and stacks (T5s)

The four roof units were plain `steel` boxes and the stacks were two cylinders. Both now have art at the code's sizes. The stack keeps the code's taper (1.6 to 1.4) and its red band height (20..21), so it reads the same from across the river. Shipped unverified.

## m734 -- security_fence.glb: the factory lot's fence (T5r)

The fence round the factory lot is about 270 m, so its weave is a cost question first. The first build made the diamonds from boxes at 1,710 faces a metre: 460k for the lot. Flat double-sided ribbons in one mesh give 166 a metre, about 45k, and still read as chain-link. It is one metre TILED, not one copy stretched along a segment, because a stretched weave smears into zigzags. The outrigger leans outside, as real security fencing does. Shipped unverified.

## m730 -- gatehouse.glb: the factory gate's hut and boom (T5q)

This was a white box with a dark lid and a glass strip, and a red bar with four white stripe boxes laid on it. The art is the same hut at the same size: the window still faces the road (-v), plus a door, a lamp, a camera and a teal company band. The boom is striped in its own geometry, with a counterweight and a rest fork. The gate itself stays `GATES`' `uplift`. Shipped unverified.

## m727 -- outfeed_tower.glb: the outfeed tower's stair and platform (T5p)

In code the tower is 32 solid `grate` blocks rising from the quay, so it reads as a wedge, plus a slab on four sticks. The art opens it up: treads at the code's exact positions on two stringers and three bents, and a braced four-leg frame under the platform. The blocks stay the colliders. A stair you can see through is the point, because the turret on the platform (`wfTurrets`) is the climber's problem. Shipped unverified.

## m725 -- halt_stairs.glb: the halts' platform stairs and the yard fence (T5o)

The stair's step count depends on the ground (`gnd` per step, up to 40), so it can't be one baked flight. The art is one step and one leg pair per step: the step at the code's .28 / .45, the legs stretched down to each block's own foot. The fence is one bay at the code's spacing (a post every 3.6 m, rails .85 and .45). Shipped unverified.

## m722 -- dock_stair.glb: the stair down into the dry dock (T5n)

Sixteen `quay` blocks, a `steel` slab and two `yel` bars. The rise was not typed: Y - floor is 4.95, read back from the m683 stair tower (deck - Y = 6.25, deck = floor + 2.2 + 9), so each riser is .309. In the preview part of the landing renders black. That is the stand-in quay's top being coplanar with it, not the model. Shipped unverified.

## m718 -- caisson.glb: the dry dock's gate (T5m)

The caisson was one `steel` box, two `yel` bars with posts, and `iron` fender slabs. Now it has a dressed deck (seams, hatches, valve wheels, bollards), the rail as one 30 m piece at the code's own post spacing, fender piles, and a stiffened river face. The face and piles are stretched in height, so their rivets were taken out: a stretched sphere is an egg. Shipped unverified.

## m714 -- pearl_span.glb: the Pearl's roof links, steel and rope (T5l)

`pearlSpan` draws each link as n segments of `pearlSeg` slabs plus `bx` posts. The art is the same unit: one 1 m segment per piece, stretched along the span and pitched per segment, so the rope bridge's sag is the code's own `pt(t)` and nothing is baked in. Everything that stretches carries detail only along its length (tread ribs, ropes, rails); the posts carry the knots and caps and are never stretched. Shipped unverified.

## m712 -- pearl_ladder.glb: one generic ladder for every `pearlLadder` (T5k)

The 21 ladders were two `dark` rails and a stack of `dark` slabs. Now `pl_rail` (stretched in height, so it carries no detail that would smear), `pl_rung` (a round bar with welded ends and tread nicks -- instanced per rung, so the .32 pitch stays the code's), and `pl_cap` (the rails bending over to two wall plates). A rust band on the rail was taken out after the preview: on a stretched piece it smears to a metre. Shipped unverified.

## m710 -- the MX tape, the road litter and the patched potholes as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5j)

`models/campaign/trackside.glb`. For the MX track: the spectator tape's stake with its knot at the code's .9, and a 1 m length of
tape that sags and twists a little, one white material for the code's red and white. For Hollow Creek's highway bridge: a clump of
road litter (a crushed can, a green bottle, a coffee cup, a flattened box, a strip of tyre tread, scraps of paper) and a patched
pothole, an irregular dark patch with a lighter edge and cracks running off it, drawn flat. Shipped unverified.

## m707 -- the freight trestle's deck and bents as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5i)

`models/campaign/trestle_deck.glb`, for the trestle `buildFreight` carries over the strait. A 6 m deck section at the code's
numbers: two beams, eight ties (one in three creosote-dark) with tie plates, the two rails at the code's 1.5 m gauge with a head, web
and foot, and outer guard timbers; and a bent with its posts at the code's +-1.1, a cap, a sill and X-braces on both faces, 1 m tall
for the code to stretch to the ground or the seabed. Shipped unverified.

## m704 -- the halts' bench, churns and lamp posts as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5h)

`models/campaign/halt_extras.glb`, for the platforms `buildFreight` dresses at each end of the trestle. The bench under the shelter
at the code's .45 x 2.4: slatted seat and back on cast-iron ends, with the green timetable board and its four lines beside it; a pair
of steel milk churns with their bands and necks and two tied mail sacks; and the platform lamp post: a lantern under a hood, its
bracket and a hanging basket of flowers. Shipped unverified.

## m701 -- the fair field's poles and bunting as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5g)

`models/campaign/fair_field.glb`, for the field `buildFairground` hangs its bunting over: the code's 6 m pole tapered, with a red cap,
three hooks where the lines tie on and a guy rope to a peg; and a pennant at the code's .4 x .45, one white material for its three
colours, on a length of cord. T5g also maps the field's hay, the trucks at the gate and the stage's flag onto pieces already in the
repo (the MX hay bale, the rally truck, the rim flagpole). Shipped unverified.

## m698 -- the MX track's start gate and hay bales as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5f)

`models/campaign/mx_extras.glb`, for `buildBikeTrack`. The start gate on the hill's front edge at the code's seven posts across the
lanes: six drop-plates with blank number boards between them, the yellow bar along the top and the starter's release lever off the
end. And a hay bale at the code's 1.5 x .9 x .85, two twine bands and loose straw. Shipped unverified.

## m695 -- the trailer park's porches and awnings as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5e)

`models/campaign/trailer_porch.glb`, for `buildTrailerPark`. The awning at the code's 2.2 x 3.2: a corrugated tin sheet falling
away from the trailer, two rust patches, on its two steel posts with a rail back to the trailer and a string of five bulbs under it;
and the porch deck at the code's 1.7 x 2.2 on four posts with a step down toward the walk. Shipped unverified.

## m692 -- the mill's saw line, log piles and sawdust as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5d)

`models/campaign/mill_floor.glb`, for `buildMill`. The saw line at the code's 21 m: a bed with yellow edges and steel rollers every
1.2, the head saw -- a toothed blade on its axle where the code puts it, under a yellow hood on four posts (the first draft boxed the
blade in out of sight), a red motor and a control box. Log piles of four and three courses at the code's spacing, bark in two tones,
cut ends with rings, on two bearers. And a sawdust heap to scale. Shipped unverified.

## m688 -- the trailer park's boardwalk as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5c)

`models/campaign/trailer_walk.glb`, for the walk `buildTrailerPark` runs along the creek. A segment at the code's 3.4 wide and 4.3 long:
planks in three weathered tones on three bearers; a 4 m rail with a post every metre, a top rail and a mid rail; a trailer platform
at the code's 4.2 wide, 1 m long for the code to stretch; and a pile with its cap, 1 m tall for the code to stretch to the creek bed.
Shipped unverified.

## m687 -- the counter-protest camp as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5b)

`models/campaign/rally_camp.glb`, for the Pearl's counter-protest camp `buildRally` pitches by Hollow Creek's road. The code's mint
tarp at 4.4 x 3.4 on its four posts, sagging a little, with guy ropes to pegs; a string of bunting in the Pearl's five pastels along
the front; the blue cooler and the pink folding chair where the code puts them; and two blank placards on sticks. Shipped unverified.

## m685 -- the scaffold up the coaster's side as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T5a)

`models/campaign/ship_scaffold.glb`, for the repair scaffold `buildWaterfront` stands against the coaster in the dry dock. Tube and
fitting: the code's 22 standards from v 30 to 60 at u +-1.4 to top + 1.1, ledgers every 1.9 m, transoms at every standard, X-braces

## m682 -- the dry dock's blocks, the quay's fenders and the ship's stair tower as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T4z)

`models/campaign/dry_dock.glb`, for `buildWaterfront`. A keel block at the code's 1.4 x 1: a concrete footing under cribbed timbers
and an oak cap, 1 m tall for the code to stretch to the 2.2 m it leaves under the hull; a quay fender at the code's 1.3 x .36 hung
on two chains, scuffed; and the stair tower beside the dock -- a grated landing on four braced posts at 6.25 (the code's 20 risers

the landing. Shipped unverified.

## m679 -- the orchard terrace's dry-stone walls and steps as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T4y)

`models/campaign/orchard_terrace.glb`, for `buildOrchardTerrace`. A 2.1 m segment of dry-stone wall at the code's .7 thickness:
five courses of rough face stones in four tones on both faces round a hearting, a coping of stones on edge, moss on its face; and
a stone step at the code's .55 x 2.0 with a worn tread. Both are 1 m tall for the code to stretch to each segment's and step's own
height. The wall came in at 2,026 faces with bevelled stones and is 486 without them, which matters at this count; and the step's
first draft had two side slabs that rendered black, now gone. Shipped unverified.

## m677 -- the rally trucks as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T4x)

`models/campaign/rally_truck.glb`, for the four pickups `buildRally` drives up the highway road and parks behind the gate. Built in
the truck group's own frame so it drops in at the origin: a lifted pickup at the code's 2.0 x 5.0, its body in one white material for
the code's four colours, the trim -- big wheels with chrome hubs, glass (the first render had the windscreen inside the cab), the bed
liner, chrome bumpers and grille, head and tail lamps, a roof light bar and two flags on poles in the bed. Shipped unverified.

## m675 -- the Mothership gauntlet's organics as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T4w)

`models/campaign/ship_gauntlet.glb`, for `buildShipGauntlet`. The ship's juice sac at the code's r 1.1: a glowing magenta bladder in
a skin cradle, eight veins over it, three feeding tubes up into the hall's wall; the lock room's glow rib, a skin rib with a glowing
seam at the code's 2.2 x .5; and a tear strand drooping from the torn floor's edge with a glowing bead at its tip. Shipped unverified.

## m671 -- the lot's chain-link fence and the channel bridge's piers as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T4v)

`models/campaign/chainlink.glb`. The city ring lot's chain-link fence: a galvanised post with its bands and a domed cap, never
scaled, and a 1 m section of diamond weave with its top rail and bottom wire for the code to stretch between posts (the first draft's

## m669 -- the creek footbridge, reeds and lilies as art (scenery window; ROADMAP T4u)

`models/campaign/farm_waters.glb`, for `buildFarmWaters`. The footbridge at the code's 14.6 x 1.6: planks on two bearers, both
handrails with a mid rail and a diagonal brace in every bay between the code's seven posts, and the two trestles at +-2.6, X-braced

## m475 -- the farm bushes (scenery window, art only; the swap is ROADMAP T2d)

Colin: *"bushes on the farm land."* `models/campaign/farm_bushes.glb`: four soft, rounded pieces in the Sites painting's greens --
`fb_hedge` (one 2.7 m hedge piece on an earth bank, the exact length of `FBOUND.piece`, so it replaces the bank ellipsoid and three
faceted ico0 clumps one for one), `fb_round`, `fb_cypress`, `fb_flower` (orange/red blooms: the five percent loud colour).
Every lump is flattened AT THE GROUND, not above it: the first render had every bush floating because the underside was clamped
relative to the lump's own radius rather than to y = 0. The hedge is subdivision 2 throughout (740 tris) because it repeats along
every field edge; the free-standing bushes can afford 3. No collider file: the hedge keeps its code box, the bushes are scenery.
Code untouched; the loop swaps it in (T2d). Shipped unverified.

## Landmines

### m825 (T6z) -- the footbridge's foot on the beach is his art
`FOOT.ffG` loads `models/campaign/foot_dress.glb` (`?ffoot=0` leaves it out). In m490's foot block, `ff()` places a node and
pushes it into `fbArt`, so it is merged with the bridge.
- **Same rolls, same order:** the flagstones and driftwood make the same `fr()` calls in the same order as before, so the
  path and the tideline land where they always did.
- **`ff_flag`:** scaled x by w and z by d / .76.
- **`ff_hut`** (yaw .15): the hut collider stays.
- **`ff_post`:** its `FF_board` material is cloned and painted red while the gap is open, white once `FT.fixed`.
- **`ff_buoy`** goes at the lifebuoy post.
- **`ff_drift`:** scaled x by the rolled length.
- **`ff_bench`** (yaw .2): the seat collider stays.

The stones, sandbags, rope posts and concrete apron stay code. Shipped unverified.

### m823 (F5-6a) -- SHADOWHIDE RANCH, the haunted ranch (`RANCH`, `buildRanch`, `ranchStep`, GOD `ranch`, roster `rancher`)
**The site** is a new farmland flat, `FARMLAND.FLATS[2]` = (160, 80) with r 32. `fpOwner` keeps fields out to 22 m.
- **(172, 112) was tried first and rejected:** `flBase` there is 0.0, a hollow by the shore, and `places` printed it 2.20 m
  off its own flat at the fence corners.
- **At (160, 80):** y 3.9, 63 m from the beach, and the fence corners are 0.87 m off the flat.
- **The frame:** +v is `FARMLAND.ub`'s bearing + .5.

**What is there:**
- A gate at v -15, two log posts with a canvas sign.
- Barbed wire on three sides: posts that do not collide, and two `pearlSeg` strands.
- The house at (-6, 5): 9 x 6, closed up, its windows boarded, a door, a tin roof as two tilted slabs, a chimney. The porch
  deck is .35 high, under the .357 step, with posts, a tin porch roof, a bench, a crate and a bulb.
- The Birch Institute's white trailer at (7.5, 5), on blocks, with a dish, a whip aerial, a generator and a cable.
- The watchtower at (9, -8): a deck at 5, rails, a spotlight and a camera. Its `pearlLadder` is on its -v face (psi PI).
- The corral at (-8, -8): a ring of 14 posts with two rails, a gap at k 3, a scorched `RingGeometry` inside, a trough, and
  three stones that bob over the ring. The stones are their own meshes, moved by `ranchStep`.
- Three skulls, a dead tree, a burn barrel.
- Four camera poles. Their red lights are one `noBatch` material that `ranchStep` blinks.
- Tully on the porch, `talk`.

**Checked:** `tools/placecheck.mjs` runs `buildRanch` and prints a `RANCH` row:
`RANCH boxes 37 | off its flat by 0.87 m | y 3.9 | from the beach 63.1 m | ladder yes`, with GOD `ranch` ok and 0 BAD.
`play ch1` passed (263 s).

**Still to do:** F5-6b (the night) and F5-6c (the ability).

### m821 (T6y) -- the footbridge's span, piers, stair and lamps are his art
`FOOT.fbG` loads `models/campaign/footbridge.glb` (`?fbridge=0` leaves it out). In `buildFootbridge`, `fb()` places a node
and records it in `fbArt`. Placements:
- **`deck()`:** keeps the deck and rail colliders and tiles `fb_bay` (2 m) n = round(L / 2) times, scaled z by st / 2, with
  `fb_post` at the run's far end. The chords, posts and diagonals are not drawn.
- **`fb_pier`** is stretched from sea - 5 to yD - .6.
- **`fb_step`** goes on each stair step's top. Measured: its yellow nosing sits on the -v side, the beach-facing edge.
- **`fb_lamp`**: his arm reaches -X, inward for s = 1, so the s = -1 lamp is turned PI.

The broken and mended spans, the stair's handrail posts and every collider stay. The art goes through `artMerge` into
`FOOT.artDraws`. Shipped unverified.

### m819 (T6x) -- two shore leftovers are his art: the islands' cliff-ladder pads and the ferry's far stair
`OFERRY.shG` loads `models/campaign/shore_steps.glb` (`?shore=0` leaves it out). It loads before `buildFerry` and
`buildIslands`, which both read it.
- **`is_footpad`** goes at every island ladder's foot pad, top on y0 + .05, turned psi. The `wood` drawing is popped.
- **`fp_tread`** goes at each of the stair's 14 treads off pier 1's tip, on the tread top, turned ps. The `plank` drawing is
  popped.
- **`fp_post`** is two per tread, ±1.1 across (local X under rotation.y ps maps to (cos ps, -sin ps) in u, v), stretched
  from the pontoon to .3 under the tread. A post is skipped where that is under .05 m.

The treads and posts join the landing's `flArt`, which is merged after commit. Every collider stays. Shipped unverified.

### m818 (T6w) -- the island gap ramp and its landing are his art
`IBASE.gapG` loads `models/campaign/gap_ramp.glb` (`?gapramp=0` leaves it out). In `buildIslandBase`'s gap ramp:
- **`grSeg` puts one `gr_seg` on each fitted segment** of `pts` (the in-run and kicker) and of `lp` (the landing, X scaled by
  landW / 3.2). Each is at R(sA, 0) on yA, with rotation order YXZ: yaw `psR`, pitch `-atan2(dy, ds)`, and `scale.z` times
  the slope length. The sign was derived, not measured: under the mirror, his +Y end lands at
  `Ry(psR) * Rx(a) * (0, 0, len)`, which needs a = -atan2(dy, ds) to rise.
- **`gr_pile`** is stretched from g - .2 to yy - .12.
- **`gr_lip`** goes on the last point.
- **`gr_gate`** goes at R(.3, 0) on y0. The gate posts keep their colliders.

The quads (the ridden surface), the canvas sign and every collider stay. The art is merged through `artMerge` into
`IBASE.artDraws`. If the segments tilt the wrong way, the sign of the pitch is the one line to flip. Shipped unverified.

### m817 (T6v) -- the swing bridge's MOVING span is his art
`OSWING.spanG` loads `models/campaign/swing_span.glb` (`?swspan=0` leaves it out).
- **Placement:** in `buildSwing`, `ss_span` is cloned, mirrored in z (`scale.z = -1`, as `campPlace` does) and added under
  `O.grp` unturned, so `swingPlace` swings it with the group.
- **What it replaces:** every drawn `add()` (deck, girder, rails, both trusses, the portal and the house) and the m418
  `mergeLeaves`.
- **Measured:** his span is ±21.6 along Y, which is `OSWING.half` exactly.
- **Unchanged:** the BDYN boxes stay the colliders, and the nose plates, barrier arms and warning lights stay code.

Shipped unverified.

### m815 (F5-5b) -- the Tall White who gets off the Phoenix Lights, and trades
When the V comes down (`PHX.st` 'down'), a procedural tall pale figure (`phxTallWhite`) stands 1.5 m off the site and turns
to face him.
- **The trade:** being within `near` 2.6 m for `hold` 2 s makes the deal.
  - It costs `price` 40 juice and buys the first of `SELL` (tank, seal, cheap, quick) that he lacks, through `goodGift`.
  - With all four owned, it fills the tank for free.
  - If he is short of juice, a card says so and he can retry 3 s later.
- **After the deal:** `phx:deal` is set (the new second step of `qphoenix`), and the lights lift `after` 4 s later.
- **Changed from m809:** reaching the site now sets `phx:seen` WITHOUT lifting the lights, so the trader has time.
- **Not a talk body:** the figure is not in `DUMMIES`, so the deal is a stand-beside, not a talk.

  `?hero=grey`).** One table entry; the start screen's row lays three cards out with flex. His file was already hashed in `ASSETS`.
  Expect `WSC.011` with no turn: his tip is pure -X, 0.157 long. Expect the `HERO grey n/n` clip chip as on the lizard. He was
  built by the same pipeline, so expect `FLAT` on his flips if his hips came over flat too (m796 handles it).

- **m796 (STEER): FLAT HIPS ARE NOT A FLIP MEASUREMENT (`flipMarks`, `AIR.flatHips` .05, `AIR.flatAir` .81, `FLIP[*].flat`).** Read
  offline from both files: zap's `front_flip` hips go 33.4 -> 59.3 -> 29.3 cm (crouch at 0, apex .333, landing .708 of .875),
  while the alien lizard's are 0.00 at all 21 keys, and his `backflip` likewise. The argmin/argmax walk on a flat track returns
  noise, so `air` was a fraction of the clip, `flipDur` ran out early and `in_air` took the weight back mid-rotation. A hips range
  under 5% of their height now returns { from 0, air .81 x dur, off 0 }. The chip's flip token now carries the action's time,
  the clip length and the weight, plus FLAT. **The lizard's missing hips translation is his retarget dropping root motion**; it is
  reported to him, not patched over. `front_flip` is in `ONCE`.

  was only right because zap's mount pair and the weapon files' pair are the same vector, (-14.3102, 0, 0), in centimetres under an
  Armature 0.01. The alien lizard's rig is in METRES, with its tip at (-0.140, 0, -0.072): 1/91 of the length and 27 degrees
  off -X. His guns were ~91x too big. The weapon group now takes `scale = |wearer| / |weapon|` and `quaternion = fromUnitVectors(weapon
  axis, wearer axis)`. **The muzzle is measured along the WEAPON's own axis in group space and then pushed through
  `group.matrix`**, so `muzzleWorld` (host.matrixWorld x muzzle) stays right. On zap the scale is exactly 1, measured: blaster and
  launcher tips -14.310176 against zap's -14.310177. This is not `weapFit` coming back: nothing is typed, both vectors are read off
  the files.

- **THE HOTHOUSE'S TWILIGHT, SPREAD AND CUT (m642, F2d-2, `HOTH.tw/every/push/cap/cut`, `hothCut`).**
  - **The twilight** damps in by how grown the player's block is. **It snapshots the fog colour and the sun and hemi
    intensities when it starts, writes from that base every frame while it is on, and restores and drops the base at zero.**
    It is never a lerp of the live value, which would creep a little further every frame.
  - **The spread:** every 40 s a random held block pushes .1 share into a random non-held 4-neighbour (`turfPush`, saved),
    up to `cap` 18 held. It toasts when a block falls.
  - **The cut:** `boltHit` calls `hothCut`. A bolt in a grown, held block takes `cut` x (.5 + charge) off `skin` there,
    spits teal sparks, and toasts when the block is lost. The save is batched (`dirty`, at most every 5 s), not one write per
    bolt.
  The melee strike does not cut yet.

  `MOVE.step * 2 + probe * 1.2` (up to a 1:1.2 slope). (2) **The board launched every kicker LEVEL**: at the lip, 16.9 m/s
  and vy -0.7 off a 25 degree kick, down 4 m past it in the sea (12 needed). Her skates had surface-following since m269
  (`bladeSurfPre/Post`: velocity along the face, a lip left on its angle) and the board never did; it does now (not the bike).
  **Both bugs were in every board ride in the game**, not just this ramp. With them fixed the driver clears the gap (102 s,
  several runs), the needle, the lighthouse. **Still open:** the keeper's Skinsuit at y -1000 (F0b-2b-4c).

One exact collider box per piece (1.25 m, the car 1.5 m) so the line is solid and hopping it is a choice, not a leak. ROADMAP T2c has the layout rule. Preview: `roadblock_kit_preview.png`.
- **CAMPAIGN DETAIL PASS, PIECE 2: THE FARM PICKUP AND TRACTOR AS MODELS (m472, `models/campaign/`).** *"There's a truck in the game, I don't know if it's supposed to be a tractor or what."* Both farm vehicles were boxes merged in code (`vehPickup`, `vehTractor`). Now: a retro 1950s pickup (rounded hood and cab, chrome grille and bumpers, round headlamps, running boards, curved fenders, a wooden bed with a hay bale and a spare tyre, cream hubs) and a classic red tractor (long hood with a chrome grille, exhaust stack, seat and wheel, big treaded rear tyres under curved fenders, small fronts, a three-disc plough). Bevelled and smooth-shaded, ~2,800 faces each, opaque except the glass. Same model space as `vehParts` (forward +z, origin on the ground) and the same footprints, so ROADMAP T2b is a load-and-swap with nothing else to change. Preview: `farm_vehicles_preview.png`. Not in the game until T2b.
- **THE BALLOON STOPS RE-WRAPPING (m471, `talkShow`, `talkLetter`, `#talk.comic`).** *"Based on how you're looking at them it's
  always adjusting the line wrap."* `#talk` was `width: auto` at a moving `left`, and a fixed box's shrink-to-fit width is the
  screen LEFT BESIDE IT -- so every camera turn changed the line breaks. It is measured once when a line opens, at `left: 0`
  (the whole screen to fit in, so `max-width` decides), and its width pinned; only `left`/`top` follow him after. **The
  lettering cannot move a break either**: the whole line is always laid out, the words not yet lettered in a
  `visibility: hidden` span. The tail is `--tail`, his projected x inside the balloon, so a balloon held off an edge still
  points at him. Comic style is on by default; the fonts come from Google Fonts with system fallbacks, so a phone offline
  gets Comic Sans rather than nothing. **A tap mid-lettering finishes the line** (the playthrough's six taps a talk still
  finish every script: ch1 18/18). **Handing off T2:** yes -- see Decisions; the level window owns `models/campaign/` art.

- **CHAPTER 3 PLAYS THROUGH, AND THE BIKER RODE FOR THE FIRST TIME (m470).** *Four game faults the playthrough found:*
  (1) **`boardBusy` refused the board to every disguise but her skates** (`p.mphK && !bladeOn()`, m263), and the biker IS a
  disguise -- so since m374 wearing him never put him on his bike, the race could never start, and `bikeOn()` read true the
  whole time. `!bikeOn()` joins the exception. **A derived state with two conditions needs both checked when a third mode
  arrives** -- the skates added an exception and the bike, one mode later, did not.
  (2) **The start hill's back was a staircase across the whole track** (`buildBikeTrack`), and the loop runs THROUGH the hill:
  lap 1 starts on top, lap 2 arrives at the back and stopped dead (0.9 m/s). It is a ramp now (h / .26 long, both windings),
  so the hill is the lap's jump. `places`' own race row said WON (it starts lap 1 and never asks about lap 2).
  (3) **A body knocked where there is no floor** (the creek under the stilts: `groundAt` -1000) fell to -1000 and stayed there
  -- a quest's biker gone. Every body remembers where it last stood (`d.okX/Y/Z`, at rest above -50) and is put back there.
  (4) **`texLoad` let `KTX2Loader.load` THROW at module scope** -- node's fetch does on a relative URL, so `npm run places` died
  at boot from m425 to now and no build since has had its place check. Caught into `onErr` now; places runs clean.
  *And one pacing fix:* the rally is called within 15 s while ch3c waits on the speech within 60 m of the stage.
  *Harness:* a race driver (`gang:respect`): the biker form, still at the gate for the countdown, then the line itself -- its
  nearest point in a window behind-to-ahead of the last one (never further back, so running wide cannot turn him round), aimed
  14 m past. The first version advanced its target only while he was near it, ran wide, turned round, and rode 2.5x the lap.

- **CAMPAIGN DETAIL PASS, PIECE 1: THE CRASH WRECK AS A REAL MODEL (m469, `models/campaign/`).** *"Develop the game land... the crash, all that stuff could be developed further."* The campaign's scenery is typed into `index.html`, which the loop owns, so the scenery window builds each piece as a GLB in `models/campaign/` (contract in `README_CAMPAIGN_ART.md`) and ROADMAP T2a asks the loop to swap it in -- art in files, code in the loop, no collisions. The wreck: a smooth 64-segment saucer (hull, dark rim, sixteen rim lights with a third dead, glass dome over a glowing core), tipped 20 degrees nose-down and sunk, a torn gash with exposed ribs and three peeled panels on the nose side, the hatch ramp open on the tail side, a bow wave of earth in front, a scorch disc and hull shards and clods behind. 3,140 tris. Three exact colliders (tail, nose, bow wave) and the six empties `CRASH.at` already reads. `models/campaign` added to `bump.mjs` DIRS. Preview: `crash_wreck_preview.png`. Not loaded by the game until T2a.

  (`npm run play ch2 --seed=N`) before calling it a game bug.

- **GLOWTIDE: THE GROUND HAS SIDES (1,013 SOLID RUNS UNDER EVERY STEP, STAIR END AND QUAY EDGE) (m467, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"I'm still walking through the sides of stairs and falling through."* The ground collider is the visual ground as WALKABLE TRIANGLES (`col_deck_ground`), and the loader keeps only up-facing ones -- so every drop in the ground (the sunken plaza's stairs, the stage, the quay edges, the canal lips) was a floor with nothing under its edge. `col_bld_ground_sides`: every 1 m ground cell standing more than 0.2 m above a neighbour gets a solid box from the lowest neighbour to its own top, merged into x-runs -- 1,013 boxes from 2,078 edge cells. Kerbs (0.12) and the beach slope stay plain floor so they can still be stepped. Route checker: 0 problems. Also on main: ROADMAP.md has the **Glowtide mechanics block (G1-G7)** for the game window -- portals, grind rails, moving platforms, hide bins, cameras, enemies, events -- gated on Colin saying "do the Glowtide block".
- **GLOWTIDE: SIX DEAD PORTALS (CHECKPOINT + FAST TRAVEL), A QUIETER SEA (m466, `models/alien_plaza/`).** The portals from MECHANISMS.md: two posts and a ring at the stage (lit from the start) and at every core's arrival -- bell room, vault, lighthouse gallery, keep summit, boathouse dome -- as `portal_N` markers (kind `portal`, `lit`, `where`). The game lights one when you reach it and lets you jump between lit ones. The sea and canal water are tinted down (.62/.74/.8) in kit mode: compose.py flagged most frames NOISY and the culprit was the saturated cyan water filling the bottom third -- the sea is the quiet 70%, the cores and bunting are the loud 5%. (Re-pushed on top of m465 from the game window, which landed between pull and push.)
- **THE KIT IS FOUND, NOT ISSUED (m465, `GEAR`, `gearHas`, `gearSync`).** *"You just wake up and you have all of the weapons.
  You shouldn't start with weapons -- you discover new technologies: a hoverboard, a jet pack, the DNA gun, your blaster, the
  rocket launcher."* In the campaign (`tkit`) a new game is BARE HANDS; each slot is his once the quest in `GEAR.get` is done:
  hammer `ch1` (Dee, the building site), blaster `ch1d` (Briggs, chapter 1's end), board `ch2c`, hover pack `ch3c`, launcher
  `ch4c`. **It is READ off the save's `qdone:` flags, never stored**, so an old save lands with what its chapter would have
  found and nothing migrates. The wheel is REBUILT from what he has (`wepRow._ix` maps a segment back to its slot); cycling
  and picking skip the rest; the hover pack is `HOVER.have && gearHas('pack')` (on by default in the kit city now, gated by
  the find). A new find gets a FOUND card 1.7 s after the quest's own. `gearSync` runs every frame (5 slots, a mask compare)
  so a GOD-marked quest updates the wheel too. Every other world has everything, and **GOD > ALL KIT** (`mel.allkit`) gives
  the campaign everything for testing. **AT BOOT `gearSync(1, 1)` SETS ONLY THE SLOT** -- `paintKit` reaches things declared
  thousands of lines below it, and a const read above its declaration is a blank page.
  **NOT DONE:** the DNA gun mode is already debug-only (m282 -- sampling is the hold); Clancy is still found at the wreck in
  ch0's first step and follows from there, which is the "rescue" as it stands; psychic / mind control / telekinesis / phasers

- **COVER IS MUTED, THE LEDGE ASKS FOR THE THUMB, AND THE HARNESS'S NaN WAS ITS OWN (m464).** *"I'm trying to go around the
  corner, he covers on a building, and you're like no... the ledge hang often catches onto ledges you don't mean to, like a tree."*
  `WALL.on` 0 by default (GOD > WALL COVER, `mel.cover` remembers it); every line of the cover system is intact behind it.
  `LEDGE.want` .35: the grab needs the stick pushed INTO the face (the cover's own cosine test), so a jump beside a wall or a
  drift past a canopy no longer hangs him; 0 is the old free catch. The double jump was already on in the campaign (m451,
  `AIR.dbl`, the second jump is `flipAir`) -- if it is missing on his phone, GOD > DOUBLE JUMP was flipped OFF and remembered.
  **THE LADDER NaN IN `npm run play` WAS THE HARNESS**: `st.sideSign` was never initialised, so the first side-step pushed
  `-undefined` into the left stick and the climb carried it into `pos.y`. It looked like a game NaN for three runs; the ring
  trace's `stick NaN` on the frame BEFORE the player's was the tell. A phone pad cannot produce a NaN, so no game guard.

(1) Every `col_bld_*` mesh held every box of its building (walls, parapets, stacks) -- the loader takes an EXACT 8/24-corner mesh as a turned box and RASTERISES anything else, so a thirty-box mesh became a sack of columns with gaps. `_raw` now writes ONE OBJECT PER BOX (`col_bld_ww1_003`; the loader strips `_NNN`): 702 colliders, 693 of them exact 24-corner boxes. (2) Stairs, bridges and the canal ledges were `col_deck_` triangle copies -- floors with no sides -- so their flanks were air and what was under them was the sea bed. They have solid box twins now (`col_bld_sea_stairs` etc.), standable AND solid. The checker found one side effect: parapet tops are surfaces now, so the twin-tower balcony (glyph 1) was a jump from wq4's parapet; it is a metre higher (hover only again). 0 problems. Also: the bell-room shortcut rail landed on the fountain -- it lands at the plaza's west corner now, rails are painted steel on end pylons with a hanger cable (not a rusty pipe), and nine more bunting runs (he likes them).

- **GLOWTIDE: EVERY KIT MATERIAL WAS EXPORTED ALPHA-BLENDED (INSIDES THROUGH WALLS, 23 FPS) -- OPAQUE NOW; PLUS MASSING JOGS, PILASTERS, THREE PARAPETS (m459, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"A heck ton of things have reversed normals, you're seeing the underside... 23 fps looking one way, 60 the other."* Not normals: m453-m458 exported all 40 of his kit materials as `alphaMode: BLEND` (the imported blend_method read as blended and `_mat_rebuild` wired the texture alpha into every one), so the game sorted 700k transparent triangles back to front -- walls drawn behind their own interiors, the fill cost of blending the whole town. Now: OPAQUE + backface culling for walls, ground and props; MASK only for ivy, leaves, decals, signs, graffiti; BLEND only for glass and water (33 opaque / 10 blend / 1 mask). Also in this build: one massing jog per block (every other building set back 0.5 m), pilasters every two bays on long faces, three parapet kinds (flat coping / corbelled / dentils), heavy dressing thinned (pipes .35, clutter .3, AC .35, ivy .6). 738k tris.
- **GLOWTIDE: THREE KINDS OF AWNING OVER EVERY SHOP DOOR (THREE OF EVERYTHING) (m458, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"Say you have three of anything: three corners, three awnings, three roofs, three bricks... and the combinations."* `kit_awnings`: over every `wall_door_*` / `wall_wide` piece in the level (129 of them) one of three awnings, chosen per building: A the flat steel canopy with slats and tie rods (his photo), B the straight fabric awning with a striped valance, C the curved drape with a scalloped front. Placed off the piece's own world matrix (outward = the wall's local -Y), so they sit on the door whatever the block's rotation. The kit rule and the massing rule (one jog per block: upper floors offset a bay, a middle third stepped out) are in STYLE_GUIDES.md; the massing is the next build. 777k tris.
- **GLOWTIDE: THE BUILDING FORMULA (PLINTH, STRING COURSES, CORNICE, COPING), SMOOTH SEA WALLS WITH A LIP AND A FOOTER LEDGE, SIDEWALK BANDS (m457, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"This building looks like it needs a header... they just look like boxes. The retaining wall is vertically sectioned... where the water meets the wall it shouldn't just be a line."* `kit_hf`: every building (his kit ones, the piece towers, the keep, the gate) gets a plinth (0.9 m, his raw brick, proud), a string course at every floor line, a cornice band under the parapet and a coping on it -- the seven-part formula read off his Portland photos is in STYLE_GUIDES.md. `kit_seawalls`: the 1 m ground cells facing a drop are chained into loops, resampled and run through a 5 m moving average (which removes the staircase; Chaikin only rounds it), then extruded with MITRED bands: a coping lip (0.6 x 0.3) and a footer ledge at the water line. The ground plan: a sidewalk band of his slabs round every block, 0.12 m up on a kerb, and a raised medallion on the bastion (`ground_at`, so the collider and the checker see it). 753k tris / 44 materials.

Streets and the promenade wear it; his sidewalk slabs stay on the quays and roofs. Done with numpy in a minute: a photo he likes is a texture.
- **GLOWTIDE: FEET ON EVERY FACE, DECALS AND GRAFFITI, ROOFTOPS DRESSED, KEEP AND GATE FROM HIS PIECES, THE SHOT CHECKER (m455, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"Everything where one plane of a box collides with the ground there should be a foot... break up the textures on the ground with decals, graffiti, moss, ivy."* `kit_feet`: every vertical face in the level whose bottom edge sits on the ground gets a sloped dirt skirt with rubble (4,068 edges: fountain, quay ledges, stairs, keep, gate, towers, every building) -- not a per-block special case. `kit_decals`: 110 cards off his street-decal atlas on the paving (manholes, cracks, patches) + a graffiti tag low on every other block; his detile shader keys ride on his ground materials into the game. Rooftops dressed (water tanks / vent stacks, planters and crates in the corners, route roofs keep their middle clear). The keep and the gate are stacked from his pieces. The piece library's `.001` twin materials are remapped onto the city's (they rendered black). Trim is his concrete, not his rusty post metal. Fountain in his tile. `compose.py` + `compose.txt`: a camera at every intended waypoint looking at the route's landmark, scored on three value bands / a foreground shape / landmark on a thirds point / 70-25-5 colour -- 16 of 21 frames still say FIX (rooftops flat, canal shots drab); that list is where dressing goes next. 752k tris / 43 materials / 12.6 MB: still a look test. MECHANISMS.md: the escape-room part catalogue and the world/star structure.
- **THREE LOOK RULES ON GLOWTIDE: NO VISIBLE FACETS, NO BOX-MEETS-PLANE LINE, A FASCIA UNDER EVERY CAP (m454, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"The things that kill me is when you can see individual polygons... it's a box meeting a plane on the ground, a perfectly straight line... Sunshine blends them."* Three rules, now in the builder for kit mode: (1) every curve (fountain, domes, lathes, tubes, the hill) is 24 segments and SMOOTH-SHADED -- faces flagged, their verts welded in bmesh so the normals average; (2) every building foot gets a sloped dirt skirt in his dirt texture with rubble cubes and weeds (`PL_foot_skirts`, no collider), and the sunken-plaza stairs lost the yellow kerb tint (they read as yellow bricks); (3) every pyramid cap gets a 0.5 m overhang on a fascia band. Still a look test, not a budget: 653k tris / 50 materials.
- **GLOWTIDE REBUILT OUT OF HIS KIT CITY (mode kit): HIS BUILDINGS, HIS GROUND, HIS PROPS ON THE SAME ROUTES (m453, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"This is exactly the kind of building I'm trying to avoid... what I think looks good [his kit city] versus what I don't."* His diagnosis was right: every wall here was a box in a costume. So the SET is swapped and the LAYOUT kept. `build_all(\"kit\")` (`aw_kit.py`) reads `toon_city_kit_buildings.glb`, `toon_city_visual.glb` and the piece library, re-fits every block of the plaza onto his 3 m bay grid with his real buildings (fronts to the street, deep blocks as two rows back to back, shared parapets removed so a block reads as one row; the two shapes his set lacks -- the 15 m tower and a 2-bay house -- are stacked from his pieces), builds the towers from his wall/corner/roof/parapet pieces, lays his sidewalk / grass / curb / asphalt on the ground, and places his palms, trees, bushes, planters, benches, lamps, bins and weeds. Every ladder, rail, platform, marker and intended waypoint is moved WITH its block (`remap_pt`, snapped onto a placed building). Route checker on the kit colliders: 0 problems (ROUTES.txt). Budget: 626k static tris / 49 materials / 10.4 MB on the wire -- a test of the LOOK, not a shipping budget; his pipes, clutter and AC units are thinned to ~40%% already. STYLE_GUIDES.md: the per-chapter checklist (ground, edge, wall, trim, roof, openings, accents, living, sky, one signature effect) with Glowtide's own set spec'd -- the kit set is a stand-in to judge the layout.
- **GLOWTIDE IN HIS ALIEN LOOK, REAL ROOF COLLIDERS, GRIND RAILS, MOVING PLATFORMS, ENEMIES WITH REASONS (m452, `models/alien_plaza/`).** *"When I'm walking on roofs... the slanted roofs it's just as if it's like a step roof and I'm falling through the roof"* -- the Blender side's fault: every pitched roof was a flat box. `col_deck_roofs` now carries every upward triangle of every building/tower/cap above 2 m straight from the visual; building boxes stop at the eaves. *"They shouldn't be ziplines, they should be grinding rails"*: `rails` in the JSON (a = high end). New `platforms` (bell lift replaces the clock ladder; a summit shuttle across a 10 m break; a harbour ferry), `enemy_walker_NN` (spore_walker, a Goomba) and `enemy_drone_NN` (buzz_drone, shoots) with patrols, reasons and behaviours in `aw`. The look is mode `alien` (`build_all(\"alien\")`): his own rusted-plate / coral / violet-glow-stone textures, non-route buildings as tank-drum clusters with mushroom caps; `art` is the old seaside look on the same layout. 22 materials, 19 images all embedded (one, rock_painted, was a greyscale PNG the WEBP export dropped -- converted to RGB). Route checker (now run on the alien colliders): 0 problems.
- **THE HOVER PACK, BUILT TO THE ROUTE CHECKER; THE DOUBLE JUMP OFF IN GLOWTIDE (m451, `HOVER`, `hoverStep`, `hoverDraw`,
  `#hover`, `AIR.dbl`, `mel.hover`, `mel.dbljump`).** LEVELS.md: hold jump in the air, 1.0 s of hover, +1.0 m of lift, refills on
  the ground. His checker's header pins the model: jump apex 2.81 (the game's 10.6 / g 20), sprint gap 7.6, **hover gap 15.5,
  hover rise 4.4**. A steady +1.0 m/s climb for 1.0 s from the TOP of the jump, then a fall from apex + 1, at 7.2 m/s, is
  0.53 + 1.0 + 0.62 s = 15.46 m -- the checker's number, so that is the model. Gesture: in the air a thumb held still on the
  RIGHT pad (inside `tapR`, past `tapT`, so a quick second tap is still a tap), dead-centre on the LEFT (`leftDead` .12: more is
  steering), or Space. A cyan meter over the juice bar; cyan puffs under his feet while it runs.
  **MEASURED IN THE REAL FRAME** (flat test floor, sprint, 60 fps): jump 7.56 m / apex 2.72; hover **15.72 m / apex 3.74**, 1.00 s.
  **THE FIRST CUT FLOATED FOR 4 SECONDS**: the start condition (vy <= 0) was asked every frame, the hover sets vy = +1, so it
  switched off, gravity took three frames to bring vy back to 0, and it switched on again -- one frame in four, the meter at a
  quarter speed, 37.6 m across. The top-of-jump test now gates the START only (`H.on ||`). (The harness's own first run was
  wrong too: a steering thumb with `far` left at 0 counts as a still one -- set `stick.L.far` like a real pad does.)
  **THE DOUBLE JUMP BEATS EVERY HOVER GATE IN THE LEVEL**, computed: 5.19 m of reach and a 12.5 m sprint gap against the 11.7 /
  10.4 m lighthouse gaps, the 3.8 m dome rim and the 4.2 m teaser ledge. The checker models ONE jump and the geometry is final
  for it, so `AIR.dbl` is 0 in the plaza (1 elsewhere); both are GOD switches, remembered. The hover is on from the start in the
  plaza until the vault event grants it (the events build). **`AIR` and `HOVER` sit ABOVE `WORLD`** -- the first cut read
  `WORLD.now` in their tables and `check:boot` caught the blank page; the per-world defaults are set right after `WORLD`.
  `npm run play`: 3 full runs, 2 clean; the third hit **`NaN in the player` in ch1.3** (the fight for Dee), the same rare NaN m430
  saw before any of this -- intermittent even seeded, hover off in that world. `play` now writes the whole trace to
  `play_fail.txt` (gitignored) so the next one keeps its frames.

The launch edge needs the hover too (the fuel cell does). 0 problems.

  (`questAvail`: `from`, `needQ`, `SAVE.ch`) -- the tool drives whatever `quest.cur` is, prints a row per step as the key
  changes, and stops when the chapter's quests are all `qdone` and `SAVE.ch` has moved on; the incursion (`qinc`, m349)
  tracks itself when its ship comes and was driven through on seed 2 (52 s, 294 m, 10 teleports) before the picker went
  back. Drivers: `skin` approaches to 40% of `r` and WAITS (the shipped test fires `virusGo` itself); `unskin` blows the
  tagged alien only when `d.st !== 'down'` (41693: the count is at the get-up, `d.downs >= qDowns`; a blow on a downed body
  punts it); a `fix` gate is walked at straight with no side-step (which left the span and reset the lean); `goTo` takes the
  target's y -- reached in xz but 1.5 m apart in y is NOT reached (seed 2 sat on a scaffold over Sal tapping at nothing for
  100 s), and a teleport lands on the target's level (`godTo(x, ty, z)`: with y null it takes the highest floor it finds,
  which beside a scaffold is the scaffold). A NaN WATCHDOG: the last 8 frames of his state in a ring; any non-finite
  coordinate fails the step with them. The row for a failed gate carries `v u fixT open lets side`.
  **THE FIX GATE WAS FRAGILE AND SEED 1 MEASURED IT.** `gatePush` (the slab): `if (Math.abs(v) >= half) { ...; G.fixT = 0;
  continue; }` with `half = GATE.t*.5 + p.r = 0.493`; `gateStep` (the mend) adds `dt` while `|v| < 1.6`. So the timer only
  accumulated while he was pressed INSIDE the slab each frame (the stick carrying him 3 mm in before the push-back), and a
  body resting at |v| = 0.52 had it zeroed every frame -- 'Fixing... 1%' flickering for 120 s, the quest never passing. The
  probe (`gateprobe.mjs`) at walk speed sat at -0.49 and mended in 2 s; seed 1 sat at -0.52 and never did. **The lean zone is
  one number now, `GATE.lean` 1.6**: the push-back resets the timer only outside it. The unseeded run had passed this step
  by luck. **A gate that only works when you are pressed into it is a gate that mostly does not work.**
  **A NaN IN THE PLAYER, ONCE.** The second (unseeded) run: after the fight for Dee, `at -60.3,NaN,-64.2` -- `talk` cannot
  pass (`|R.y - P.y| < 1.5` is false), `godTo` cannot fix it (`dy = gy - NaN`). Not reproduced on seeds 1-3. The watchdog is

  with a NaN direction), the ledge/wall writes, `groundAt` on a degenerate triangle.

- **m421 HID EVERY BODY PAST 45 m, AND THE MEASURE COULD NOT SEE IT (m422, F0a-2g, `perfRegBodyParts`, `PERF.partFrac`).**
  The parts cull registered any mesh of a body whose `geometry.boundingSphere.radius x matrixWorld scale` was under .45 m.
  For a skinned Mixamo rig that product is ~0.01 m for the WHOLE MAN: the geometry is the authored metre-scale mesh (a
  hick's sphere 0.67), the matrixWorld carries the armature's 0.01 x the rig scale (0.0206), and the bones undo the 0.01
  at x100 -- the size is in the skinning, not in either matrix. The skinned sphere (`skeleton.update();
  computeBoundingSphere()`) is no better at spawn (no pose yet: the same 0.01) and 60 after a frame. **So every body's main
  mesh went into the cull and was moved to layer 1 past 45 m.** The tool's `bodies <drawn>/<near>` reads `root.visible`
  and said 74/74 while 50 of them were invisible; its `who` showed the crowd as `construction_worker 44` one run and
  `construction_worker 20` the next, which I read as the cull working. **A COUNT THAT DOES NOT MEASURE THE THING IT NAMES**
  -- the fourth time this repo has been caught by one, and the first I shipped.
  The size is RELATIVE now: the biggest geometry sphere in the body is the body; a part is anything under `partFrac` (.25) of
  it. Measured (`scratchpad/sph.mjs`, kept as `tools/bodies.mjs`? no -- the composition is in this note): the officer's
  eyes are 6% of him, Colin's trainers 21%, headphones 24%, teeth 13%, his head 43% and Moussa's head 28% -- heads stay. Most
  kinds are ONE mesh (hick, hobo, activist, hippie, hipster, biker, suit, Trump, the two women, the worker, Clancy); the
  officer is 2 (eyes), the warrior 2 (the mace), Moussa 2, Jack 2, Colin 6. A one-mesh body still measures ~2 draws in

  cell-batched set (`kitBatch`'s meshes per material per 48 m cell; `farmBatch`'s per material per 200 m cell) gets its
  cells merged once more into one mesh per material -- the far copy -- and `cellStep` decides per frame, per set, by the
  lens's distance OUTSIDE the set's rectangle (`L.out`): far -> the copies draw and every cell is off; else the cells draw
  and the copies are off. One writer (the cells' `visible` was already `cellStep`'s; `userData.lodOf` / `lodFar`).
  **THE FARM'S BATCHES SPAN THE WHOLE MAP** -- every farmFrame of every region goes through `farmBatch` -- so the first cut,
  one far copy for all of them, was NEVER far from the lens (its rectangle is Weirdport) and 21 MB of copies drew nothing.
  Now a copy per 200 m cell (`userData.fbCell`, parsed off the bucket key), FLAT: one shared `flatShading` vertex-colour
  material, no normal attribute (the shader takes the normal off the triangle), a third fewer bytes, the paint/metal/
  emissive keys folded (gone at 180 m). The kit's copy keeps its materials: `tcTint`/`kitCutMat`/`kitWobMat` hook them
  through `onBeforeCompile`, which `clone()` does not carry, so a flat kit copy would lose the city's tint.
  `mergeLeaves(G.g, flames + planks)` on every gate (46 grey posts at Old Town's cordon were 46 draws; `gateStep` only ever
  toggles the whole group).

  **THE SETTLE RUNS `perfStep` NOW.** The m417 body cull lives in `perfStep`, which the game's loop calls; the tool's settle
  did not, so the FIRST place measured in a run still had every body drawn (hctrail 801 with `--at=hctrail` first, 416 when

- **THE FAR CULLS (m417, F0a-2a, `PERF.bodyFar`, `KIT.partFar`, `cellReg(m, ownFar)`, `npm run worlds --who`).** The measure
  grew a WHO: `renderBufferDirect` wrapped for the one frame, every draw counted by the object's name (digits out), else its
  material's name, else the nearest named ancestor's. The first `--who` of the kit city said the same thing at every place:
  `kitInst 98` (every instanced door/lid/AC set, `frustumCulled = false` since m180 and never culled by distance either) and
  ~400 draws of bodies (`hick_MIX 46, construction_worker 44, fat_hipster 38 ...`) -- from the farm, the mill and the
  Mothership's core alike. **THE KIT CITY'S FOG IS 950 m** (`KCITY.fog`, so the skyline reads from the farm), so the fog
  cull (`cellStep`) hides nothing inside Weirdport; everything that is small needs a distance of its own.
  Bodies: in `perfStep`'s loop, `d.root.visible` off beyond `bodyFar` from `camera.position` (the root, so sprites and props
  go with it), and `d.seen` cleared so a hidden body animates at `animHz`. Nothing else toggles `d.root.visible` (the virus
  and the morphs toggle `model.visible`, a child). Parts: `kitInst` computes each set's sphere, pads it 3 m for a door's
  swing, turns `frustumCulled` on, and registers it with `cellReg(im, KIT.partFar)` -- `cellStep` now honours a per-mesh
  `userData.ownFar` under the fog's. Every `farmFrame` merge is named `tag:material` so `--who` can name the rest.
  **`partFar` LANDED IN `TCITY` FIRST**: a `fog:` line matched in two objects and the replace took the first; `KIT.partFar`
  read undefined and the cull was silently off. Checked by printing the owning `const` of the inserted line.

- **THE MEASURE (m416, F0a-1, `perfMem`, `PERF.mem`, `PERF.bootMs`, `mel.mem()`, `npm run worlds`, `tools/worlds.mjs`).**
  `perfMem` walks the scene's materials (every map slot, shader uniforms, `scene.environment`/`background`), counts each
  texture once at its RESIDENT size -- a KTX2 `CompressedTexture` at the byte size of its mip chain, anything else at
  w x h x 4 (x 4/3 with mips, x faces for a cube) -- and every geometry at its attributes' bytes. The chip's perf line
  runs it every `PERF.memEvery` (3) s. `renderer.info.memory.textures` is higher than the material count (327 vs 147 in
  the kit city): render targets, the PMREM chain and the shadow map are GL textures no material names.
  **`npm run worlds` DOES NOT WAIT FOR THE GAME'S OWN FRAME LOOP.** Under SwiftShader a frame runs seconds (or none in a
  minute), and the first version's 2.5 s settle read the THREE camera where the LAST place had left it -- pearl and overlook
  came back identical to the triangle. `godPlace` moves `cam.pos`; only `stepCam` copies it into `camera`. So after
  `mel.go` the tool calls `stepCam(1/30)` ten times and `cellStep()` itself, then renders one frame and reads `info`.
  A settle-in-frames version (`info.render.frame` + 3, 60 s) never saw a frame at any place and was thrown out.

     the storm table allows: `floor(20 / (stormEvery[1] + stormLast[1]))` = 3. Derive a pass mark from the table, not
     from what usually happens.

- **FLASHPOINTS (m413, D5b, `TFLASH`, `FLASHSAY`, `flashFree`, `flashPick`, `flashStart`, `flashEnd`, `flashStep`).** **`FLASH` WAS
  TAKEN** (the muzzle-flash pool, m94, line ~11135): the first insert was a `SyntaxError: Identifier 'FLASH' has already been
  declared` that `npm run check` caught before anything else did -- a blank page. Grep the name before declaring a const.
  The bodies are BORROWED, not spawned: `flashFree` is `smartFree` without the alien test (the Skinsuits push too) plus
  `!d.smart`, `!d.fp`, and no `markId` but a walker's, and `turfBodyF(d) === f`. They walk with `protestTo` (the
  protest's own steering: `pT`, `route`, `rx/rz`, `roamT = 0`) and carry `protestSign` placards; `flashEnd` takes back
  ONLY what it gave (`fpSign`, then `pT`/`route` cleared and `roamT` set, as `homeAll` does). The push is `rate x step x

  walk down the outfeed tower's stair, fall in to a LINE-UP of five on the quay behind the dry dock facing the dock. The
  STATIONS fire in order as each passes (`wfStation`): the scanner (green sparks), the strip-down (the docker's hat comes
  off), the arms (sparks, clang), THE CHROME BOOTH (Uplift's tint, `role: 'cyborg'` so `cyborgStep` builds his parts, his
  talk turns to `UPLIFT.lines`, a hiss), the visor arch (the red ring, `rosterProp`). After `stand` (45 s) in the line-up,
  with him 30 m from both ends, one goes back to the queue a docker again (`wfUnconvert`: colours, parts, visor, hat, lines).
  **A RIDER HAS NO BRAIN**: `wfRide` sits in `stepDummies`' passenger line beside `stepPack`/`stepRide`/`motoSeek`, so
  the line is the ONE writer of his position. A hit (any state but idle/walk/line) releases him for good (`lost`): a docker
  knocked off is a docker, a cyborg knocked off is a cyborg that `cyborgStep` reverts after its knock-downs. **NOTHING
  FLEES OFF A BELT**: fear is `fleeT`, not a state, and the line ignores it while it has him.

  joint, a SEAT marker), ridden round a ring in the test site only (`MOTO`) -- so it is loaded a second time in the kit city
  as the PLAYER'S (`PBIKE`, its own record; `buildMoto` is left alone because `MOTO.up` drives the ring bike). The physics
  is the board's, Rollergirl's pattern: `mode: 'bike'` on the BIKER kind, `bikeOn()` (worn, finished becoming him, the
  bike loaded, the kit city), `boardOut()` true, `p.bike` beside `p.blade`, and `stepSkate`'s numbers `BIKE` over `SK8`:
  a THROTTLE in place of the push stroke (`acc` 8 while the thumb points the way he is going, tapering to `top` 27 against
  the board's 19), a long roll, a hard brake, slower steering at speed, a smaller pop. OFF on a bike: both pads' flicks
  (`boardFlick` eats them -- no deck tricks, no body flips, no dismount: revert to walk, the skates' rule), the grind catch
  and the second jump. Drawn under him on his floor along his heading, LEANING into the turn, the fork STEERED by `MOTO`'s
  wheelbase arithmetic (`atan(L w / v)`, clamped at 20 degrees), the wheels at distance over the measured radius. He SITS:
  his root lifted by the seat's measured height (`PBIKE.seat`, off the seat bone) less his hips' height over his root in the
  driving clip, read off his posed skeleton a frame late (`stepRide`'s m109 rule), and his three driving clips blend by how
  hard it steers, summing to 1 (his idle if a clip is missing -- never a zero table, which is the T-pose).
  **`fat_biker_01` AND `fat_biker_02` FOLD TO ONE FORM NAME** (`mphFold`: "FAT BIKER"), and `mkrKind` returns the BIKER
  table (02, the one with the driving clips) first -- so Hollow Creek's bikers were already him. They say 02 now, the
  quest's sample says 02, and `places` fails a Hollow Creek biker who is not him.
  **UNVERIFIED, AND THESE ARE THE PHONE'S QUESTIONS**: which way it leans (`mel.MOTO.lean` negative flips it, shared with

  turn the right way, and whether the form wheel's FAT BIKER is the BIKER table (it should be: the same first match).

  **THE START HILL'S STEPS ARE BUILT DOWN TO THE GROUND AT THEIR OWN FOOT**: measured off the ground under the platform,
  the land behind it fell away and the first riser was a wall -- `walkUp` read `start hill 0.04 (of 1.3)`. Now each step
  is laid back from the platform at a riser of at most .3 until it meets the ground under it.

  mark's `K` false, not one body spawned, ever. `mphName(K)` is 'HOBO' / 'HICK SKINNY' (alien prefix and number off, `_`
  to space, upper case); `mkrKind` looked up `MKR.alias` ('hobo' -> 'hobo_01') and compared THAT to it raw. Never equal,
  never a prefix. So since m293 **every** `npc_*` marker -- his from Blender as much as the farmhands -- placed nothing,
  and the note `MKR NPC <id> kind?` went to the chip where nobody looked. The stem now goes through the same fold as
  `mphName` before the compare.

  whether they became anybody. It now runs `mkrNpcPlace` and fails a mark with no kind (`WITH NO KIND`):

- **WHO TALKS TO WHOM: A GROUP PER FORM, A BRUSH-OFF LINE FOR THE WRONG SORT, THE ALIEN RUN OFF (m332, B1f-3, `SOCIAL`,
  `socialGroup`, `socialMe`, `socialOk`, `socialBrush`, `QUESTS[].from`).** GAME_DESIGN "soft social friction". Every form
  is in a group off its name (`SOCIAL.groups`, regexes on `mphName`: country, street, law, worker, city, biker, crew,
  alien, else folk); undisguised you are 'alien' (`fearLooks`, the same test the fear uses). A speaker has `group`
  (default its kind's), `talks` (the groups it talks to properly; default its own) and `alien` ('flee' default, or
  'brush'), off its mark's props -- so his Blender `npc_*` markers can carry `group`, `talks` (comma list) and `alien`.
  - **The wrong sort** gets ONE line from `SOCIAL.BRUSH[their group][yours]` (else `.any`), `tap ×`, and it is over: not
    finished, nothing heard, no rumour, no `talk:` in the save. Light, never mean ("You lost? The coffee place is forty
    miles that way.").
  - **The alien**: m278's "a speaker with something unsaid does not panic" now only holds for `alien: 'brush'` -- by default
    a speaker runs from the alien like anyone (A4's fear). One who brushes him off gets the alien line.
  - **A task can come FROM somebody** (`from: '<talk id>'`): it is not available until that script is finished -- which
    only happens in a form he talks to. "Only a farmhand will get anything out of old Mabel."
  - The farmhands are `country` and talk to `country` and `street` (they are hobo bodies with farm jobs; a tramp gets a
    chat, a hipster gets the coffee line).
  **Checked headless**: Wendell existed (he never had), the alien got "Nope. Not today. Not ever.", wearing the hick he
  told his three lines and the rail-bridge rumour -- `talk:mk_farmhand_wendell` and `rm:trestle` saved. Chip `SOCIAL.brushes`.

- **RUMOURS: HEARD AS A SCRIPT'S LAST LINE, A ROUGH RING ON THE MAP, FOUND BY GOING THERE (m331, B1f-2, `RUMOURS`,
  `rumourHear`, `rumourStep`, `rumourCircle`).** GAME_DESIGN: "vague ... a separate list with no marker, or at most a
  rough circle on the map ... often how the best stuff is found". A rumour is a row: `title` (the card and the list),
  `gist` (what you remember), `say` (the line somebody tells it in), `at` (the place, read LIVE -- the crop circle off
  `FPLAN.crash.circle`, the trestle's farm end, the ford), `r` (how close counts as found) and an optional `circle`.
  - **Heard**: a mark's `rumour` APPENDS `say` to that person's lines (a copy -- a `TALKS` script is shared) and finishing
    the conversation calls `rumourHear` -> `rm:<id>` = who said it, a RUMOUR card. The farmhands carry three: Dale (the
    wheat) the ring in the wheat, Wendell (the west hill) the old rail bridge, Earl (the plough) the cows' way over
    the water. `hillman` is in the table for B1f-4's neighbour to give out.
  - **Listed**: the task list's RUMOURS section, the gist in quotes and who said it; found ones under DONE. Not
    followable -- no beam, no waypoint, no objective line. That is the whole difference from a task.
  - **On the map**: a dashed sky ring and a '?' on the FULL map only, its centre pushed .45 r off the true spot in a
    direction fixed per rumour (a hash of the id) -- so it says "round here", and the same thing every time you open it.
  - **Found**: twice a second (`rumourStep`, after `questStep`), within `r` of the place -> `rmdone:<id>`, RUMOUR FOUND,
    a task's worth of juice. Chip `RM<heard>/<found>`. GOD -> HEAR EVERY RUMOUR.

- **TASKS: SEVERAL AT ONCE, ONE FOLLOWED, A CARD WHEN ONE ARRIVES, AND THE SAME METRES IN THREE PLACES (m330, B1f-1,
  `questAvail`, `questTrack`, `tasksOpen`, `questWpt`, `#tasks`, `#wpt`).** GAME_DESIGN "Direction and discovery": a task
  comes from someone, a card pops up ("New task: ..."), it goes in your list, and you get a map marker and a waypoint
  in the world that shows the distance.

    the one everything follows is `SAVE.flags.qtrack`, else the first. m278 ran "the first one not done" only.
  - **The card**: the first frame a task is available and not `qseen:` in the save, `cardShow('NEW TASK', title)` --
    once ever, one card at a time (`newT` = the card's own life + .4 s).
  - **The list**: tap the objective pill (it takes pointer events now, `stopPropagation` so a tap is never a pad touch)
    or GOD -> THE TASK LIST. ON THE GO, each with its current step and, on the followed one, the metres; tap one to
    follow it. DONE below, greyed.
  - **The waypoint's distance in the world** (`questWpt`, after the camera, beside `skylineStep`): a gold label 2.4 m
    over the beam's target; off screen or behind, pinned to the side the target is on (camera-space x) with an arrow.
    **`quest.d` is the one number** the label, the objective line and the full map's gold dot all print -- "the map
    marker matches it" by construction (the minimap only keeps its rim dot: it turns, and text on it would too).
  - Steps can name a place READ LIVE: `at: () => [x, y, z]` on `reach`, `() => [x, z]` on `goto` -- so a task can point
    at the silo's landing or the bridge's checkpoint without a typed coordinate.

    so the list has two to choose between. GOD -> THE STAND-IN TASKS.
