- **THE STAMPEDE: A PANIC SPREADS THROUGH THE HERD, A RUNNING COW IGNORES ITS FIELD AND RUNS HIM DOWN (m329, B1e-3,
  `cowPanic`, `cowFright`, `cowSpook`, `COW.stampede` ...).** REGIONS' signature system for the farm: "cows wander, panic
  and stampede when frightened, and block lanes". On the m294 brain (graze / look / walk / trot) a fourth state, `run`:
  - **What frightens a cow**: a SHOT -- `fireBolt` calls `cowFright(muzzle, fearR 34)` -- and the ALIEN, undisguised
    (`fearLooks`, the same test the humans' fear uses), within `alienR` 6 m. A man in a human form running past still
    only startles it into the old trot. There is no shared "noise event" in this game; `cowFright(x, z, r)` is the
    cows' own, and anything else loud (a blast, a cop's pistol) is one call to it.
  - **It spreads**: `cowPanic` sets every herd-mate within `spreadR` 14 m that is not already running to `spook` after
    `spreadT` .15-.7 s, along the SAME heading (+-.25 rad) -- so a herd bolts as a herd, in a ripple, not as one cow.
  - **Running**: the target runs 8 m ahead along the flight heading, wavering +-.3 rad; `stampede` 5.6 m/s (faster than
    he jogs, slower than he sprints), turning 3x a walk, easing off over the last 2 s of `panicT` 7-11 s. **It ignores its
    field** (no `fpOwnAt` test while running) -- through the gaps, out onto the tracks and the lanes, which is "block
    lanes" -- then walks back toward its field when the panic is spent (and may well stand at a fence a while: that is
    a cow). Walls, fences and drops still stop it: a running cow that meets one TURNS (+-1.3 rad, alternating by index)
    instead of dropping to graze. Brown dust off its heels every .3 s within 60 m (the smoke pool), a high short bellow
    every 1.4-3.5 s (`mooAt` x1.32), head low, a bigger bob and a full leg swing.
  - **It runs him down**: in the bulk shove, a running cow `playerHurt`s him -- 7 damage, push 7 along its run, a
    knock-down -- once per cow per 1.5 s. GOD takes no damage (playerHurt returns), so to feel it, leave GOD.
  GOD SWITCHES: **SPOOK THE NEAREST HERD (STAMPEDE)** (`mel.cowSpook()`); `mel.cowFright(x, z, r)`. Chip: `COW..p<panics>
  h<hits>`. **`places` now spooks a herd before it ticks the farm's steps**, so the 30 frames of `cowStep` run the
  stampede branch -- a throw there is caught by `frame()` and freezes every frame after it.

- **THE ORCHARD TERRACE IS BUILT UP, NOT CUT IN: FOUR STONE TIERS ON THE ORCHARD'S OWN OUTLINE (m328, B1e-2, `FTERR`,
  `buildOrchardTerrace`, `ftRad`, `ftEdge`, `ftIn`).** Measured first (a throwaway probe on the places harness): the
  orchard stood on a 1.6 m swell (1.35..3.02 m over 2,580 m2) -- nothing to cut a terrace into. So the tiers are BUILT:
  tier 0 at the highest ground inside it + .3, each next one `rise` 1.4 m up (3.33 / 4.73 / 6.13 / 7.53), the

  **The outline is the field's, measured**: from the seed, `NT` 96 directions, march out while `fpOwner` gives the orchard
  at the point AND `margin` 3 m past it, then smooth twice (a 1-2-3-2-1 kernel: a noisy owner border would be a
  saw-toothed wall). Upper tiers are that outline x (1 - .22k). Base radius 13.7..34.8 m. `TERRACE NO ROOM` if under 6.
  **Walls**: dry-stone boxes every 1.8 m along each outline (360 samples, arc-length stepped), turned along it, from the
  tier below (or the ground - .4) to the tier top + a .25 lip; moss on the coping of ~half. **Stairs**: one flight a tier
  at `stepAt[k]`, nudged within +-.6 rad to the WIDEST ring there (the flight must fit on the tier below), .28 m risers,
  and the wall leaves a gap exactly its width. The way up winds round the hill.
  **The tops are walkable triangles (`isleAppend`), wound UP by a cross-product test** -- `triAdd` keeps up-facing floors
  only and `flWorld` is a reflection of (a, b), so the winding is derived per triangle, never assumed. They draw with the
  farmland's OWN material (`aSplat` all grass, `aFld` the orchard's tint), so the terrace grass is the same grass.
  **Built after `buildFarmWaters`, before `buildFieldBounds`** -- and the apple trees after the tops are in `TRI`, so

  more often than not -- and the terrace plants its own: a ring down the middle of each tier every ~5.5 m (off walls and
  stairs by `ftEdge` 1.9), a ring and a centre tree on top; 54 trees, six apples in every crown and two in the grass,

  **Cost**: FBATCH static tris 114k -> 184k (the crowns are ico-1, ~550 tris a tree), draw calls unchanged (batched:

- **THE COWS ARE ROUNDED AND THE HERDS GRAZE TOGETHER (m326, farm polish 5, `COW.round`, `COW.herdP` / `herdR`, `cowPick`,
  `FHERDS`).** The herd shot: two brick cows a long way apart on an empty hill. Two causes, two fixes:
  1. **every part was a unit BOX** (m294: one `InstancedMesh`, 16 instances a cow). It is now a ROUNDED box -- a unit box
     cut 2 x 2 x 2 with each vertex pulled `round` .5 of the way to the sphere through the face centres
     (`v * (1 - k + k * .5 / |v|)`: a face centre is exactly on both, so the part still fills its unit cube and every size
     in `cowDraw` means what it meant), `toNonIndexed` + flat normals. 48 triangles a part instead of 12: 39 + 3 cows x 16
     parts x 48 = ~32k, one draw call still. `COW.round = 0` is the old boxes (wants a reload).
  2. **a herd was five independent random walks over a whole field** (`cowPick` picked anywhere in its home radius, which
     is the field's). Now 70% of picks (`herdP`) are within `herdR` 7 m of a random herd-mate, and at build each cow after
     the first starts near an earlier one -- so a herd is a herd. The field test still applies to every pick (places:
     `COWS 39 ... all in their pastures`). Herds grew a little: far hill, ridge, east 7; pond 5.
  Judged with the new `npm run shot herd` (and `house`, whose camera lands in a tree -- a shot row, not a game bug).

- **THE HEDGE BANKS ARE MOUNDS, NOT BOXES; THE BOX IS ONLY THE COLLIDER NOW (m324, farm polish 3, `buildFieldBounds`,
  `buildLane` `banks` / `bankProf` / `bankEnd`).** m321's road shot: every bank a hard earth slab with vertical sides.
  Two builders, two fixes, one rule -- **`bx(...)` then `parts[mat].pop()` keeps the collider and drops the slab**, and
  something softer is drawn in its place:
  1. **the field hedges (FPLAN, 380 pieces)**: an ellipsoid (`ico1`) along the run, half-length (piece + 1.7) / 2, so
     each overlaps its neighbours by ~40% and the line reads as ONE lumpy bank; top at ~g + .46 against the collider's
     g + .45. Three clumps instead of two, at jittered heights, so the hedge's top line wanders.
  2. **the lane's sunken banks (1.9 m, walked on)**: a shouldered PROFILE run along the piece -- the foot spreads .55 m
     past the collider each side, the TOP keeps the collider's full width (so standing on the edge never floats over a
     visual slope), the crown .1 m proud. Built once per (W, H); **every face turned outward by a convexity test**
     (face centre minus the axis, dotted with the normal), not hand-ordered winding -- the profile is convex, so the
     test is exact. And **where a run starts or stops** (the lane's ends, the gaps at the barn's doors) an ellipsoid
     rounds it off: the flat cut end of the first piece was the most box-like thing left in the shot.
  Judged with `npm run shot town` (three passes: slab, profile, profile + ends) and `ridge`.

- **THE METROPOLIS ON THE HORIZON: A SCALED HOMOTHETY ABOUT THE LENS, ONE DRAW CALL (m323, farm polish 2, `SKYLINE`,
  `buildSkyline`, `skylineStep`).** m321/m322's shots: from the west hill the island city is a thin low strip, and from
  the crash site the hedges hide it entirely -- its buildings are two and three storeys at ~450 m (~3 deg over the
  horizon) and a 2 m hedge 30 m off stands 4 deg. Pushing the fog out would not have helped: there is nothing tall to
  see. **REGIONS says what the skyline IS**: the farm is the rural ring and the horizon is THE METROPOLIS -- skyscrapers,
  Dump Tower, "the skyline the aliens control from the top of Dump Tower". So it stands `dist` 1500 m past the island's
  middle on the line from the farm through it (centre (-1318, -718)), and from the fields the island city sits in front.
  **Placed by the table**: five DISTRICTS (core, The Pearl, Old Town, the waterfront with four cranes, the hill with the
  radio mast), each a named spot along the horizon with its reason, towers rolled inside it from seed 323; DUMP TOWER
  640 m, gold, three setbacks, a pulsing green beacon (it cuts the haze: k x .25) and a needle. 153 boxes, merged.
  **Its true distance (~2 km from the farm) is past every far plane here** (400 in the city, ~1,100 on the farm), so
  each frame (`skylineStep`, after `gradeStep`) the group is pulled toward the camera to `R` .86 x `camera.far` and
  scaled by the same k: world = cam + (true - cam) * k. **Every point keeps its exact bearing and angular size**, so it
  has real parallax as he walks, and depth still sorts it BEHIND the island and the hills (it sits at .86-.92 of far).
  Its own `ShaderMaterial`: per-vertex colour shaded off the sun's direction at build (sunlit faces warmer), floor
  bands and a lit window per ~16 cells, and its own haze -- `mix(c, scene.fog.color, haze * (1 - clear * h/400))`,
  thickest at the foot (`haze` .55, tops at .275) -- because scene fog would erase it. Tone-mapping and colour-space
  chunks at the end like `isle_water`. Every tower runs down to y -60 so its foot meets the water or the haze.
  **Tuned with `npm run shot`** (new rows `skyline` -- from the crash toward the city -- and `overcity`): haze .6 washed it
  into the pink; .46 made it read near and black; .55 sits it in the air. Lit windows at 12% read as night: 6%.
  GOD SWITCHES has **METROPOLIS ON THE HORIZON ON/OFF** (the A/B); `mel.SKYLINE` is live (`haze`, `clear`, `R`).
  `places` builds it and ticks `skylineStep`: `SKYLINE 153 boxes, centre [-1318,-718] one mesh`.
  **Not built: it is not reachable** -- it is the last region; nothing here pretends otherwise.

- **THE PATCHWORK READS FROM THE RIDGE NOW: A WARM FIELD DYES THE GRASS, IT DOES NOT MULTIPLY IT (m322, farm polish 1,
  `isleLandMat` FLD block, `FPLAN.dye`, `FPLAN.TINT`).** m321's ridge shot: every far field the same lime green.
  **Lime times gold is still lime** -- m308's tint MULTIPLIED the grass texture, so wheat [1.8, 1.38, .55] on a
  lime texel came out (.81, 1.03, .08), a yellower lime, and the crops (which carry the real colour) fade out with
  distance, leaving only the ground. Now, on the farmland only:
  1. the grass as a whole is taken a fifth of the way to grey and warmed (x 1.06, 1, .86) -- REGIONS' "golden
     countryside, straw", not acid lime;
  2. a tint whose red beats its green (wheat, hay, stubble, plough, the gouge, the scorch, the circle) DYES: the
     grass's LUMINANCE times the tint times `FPLAN.dye` (1.05), blended in by `(r - g) * 5`; a green tint (corn,
     pasture, orchard, reserve) multiplies exactly as before.
  So of 23 fields, 11 are warm (5 hay now STRAW, 3 wheat gold, 1 stubble, 2 plough brown with their furrows) and 12
  green, and corn [.62, .88, .42] is darker than pasture instead of the same. **Judged with `npm run shot ridge`**
  three times (before, dye .8, dye 1.05 + warm base), which is what the STEER's screenshot permission is for.
  `mel.FPLAN.dye.value` is live (a uniform); the TINT table wants a reload (it is baked into `aFld`).
  The GLSL is inside a JS template literal: **no backticks in its comments** (the first draft had them escaped, which
  is legal JS and was taken out rather than trusted to the GLSL preprocessor).

- **STEP 8, PROVED: `npm run places` AND THREE SCREENSHOTS, AND THE SCREENSHOT TOOL WORKS NOW (m321, `tools/shot.mjs`,
  `npm run shot`).** m295 dropped a screenshot tool because `page.screenshot` waits for the compositor to produce a
  frame and the kit city under SwiftShader takes longer than its 30 s timeout. **This one never asks the compositor**:
  it renders inside `page.evaluate` and reads the canvas with `toDataURL` in the SAME task, before the drawing buffer is
  cleared (no `preserveDrawingBuffer` needed). Boot ~25 s, one shot ~25 s, three in about 100 s. It serves the SHIPPED
  `index.html` and splices in exactly one thing, `window.__shot = { renderer, scene, camera }` in front of `mel`. Each
  shot is a row in `SHOTS`: a GOD place to stand at (`mel.go`), a settle time so the frame loop's steps (flora chunks,
  grade, culling) run round him, and a camera computed in the page from live state. Output to `shots/` (gitignored) or
  `SHOT_DIR`. Playwright is the global one (`/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright`), Chromium from `/opt/pw-browsers`.

  The third way over the channel and the lowest: flat stones a stride apart (`gap` 1.75 m) from the beach below the
  east pasture (`from` in the land's own (a, b)) out to the city's shore at bearing `toDeg` 79, the ray's coast
  point less 2 m, meandering `bow` 14 m off the straight line on a sine so it reads as a path found rather than
  laid. **Each stone is a box collider with its top just over the sea** (sea + .22, jittered +-.06) standing on the
  REAL seabed (the higher of `flHeightAt` and `isleBedAt`, floored at sea - 12, the trestle's own rule), drawn as a
  squat icosahedron top on a seven-sided cylinder, with weed at the waterline on about a third. Between them is the
  sea, and the sea's rule puts you back. A stone whose bed is over sea + .6 is skipped: on dry beach the shore is
  the step. **A stretch is under the tide** (`washed` .44-.6 of the way): `FFORD.gapM` measures it at **26.1 m** on
  a 172 m crossing, which nothing on foot clears (`MOVE.jump` 10.6 / g 20 is ~7.4 m at a run), so the checkpoint
  still teaches and it opens later. **Three cows stand drinking at its foot** -- `buildCows` puts them at `from` + 8 m
  in b with no field, so they are not counted against a pasture; `COWS` 33 still all in place.

  comes down a short ramp into the island's ring behind a house whose back fence is BROKEN (`FRING` row at 346 deg,

- **THE FARM'S STATIC MESHES ARE BATCHED BY PAINT KIND AND CELL (m318, STEER step 7, `FBATCH`, `farmBatch`, `fbKey`, `farmPaintKind`).**
  Every builder since m288 works in its own `farmFrame` with its own materials and `commit` merged per material only
  WITHIN that frame: 108 static meshes, a draw call each, most in view from a hill with the fog at 950. After every
  frame-based builder (`buildCityRing` is the last), `farmBatch` takes each mesh `farmMerge` made (`userData.fbatch`,
  set there and nowhere else -- so the windmill's head, the washing, cows, vehicles and crops are never touched),
  BAKES its material colour into vertex colours (THREE's colours are already linear, which is what a vertex colour
  is), and re-merges it TRIANGLE BY TRIANGLE (each to the 200 m `cell` its centre is in) into one mesh per key:
  paint kind (`FP_KIND`, or none), metal or not, glow colour. 108 -> 71 meshes over 13 materials, the camera culling
  by cell. **The paint still lands**: `farmPaintKind` is `farmPaint` with the kind given (the shader reads WORLD
  position and normal, and baked geometry is in the world with an identity matrix).
  **Left out on purpose** (`fbKey` null, 7 meshes): a map (the signs), transparent (glass, wire, water), not
  FrontSide (the hay barn's roof), already vertex-coloured -- and two whole frames (`skip`): the crash's and its
  debris's, whose GLOW is animated through their materials and would stop pulsing in a batch.
  **Colliders are untouched** -- `BOXES` were filed at each `commit`; the batch only moves what is drawn.
  `?batch=0`, or GOD's FARM BATCHING switch (reloads), builds the farm unbatched for the A/B. Chip `B<before>><after>`.
  STEER step 7 with m309's crop chunks and distance fade: done.

- **THE CITY STARTS THIN ON ITS OWN RING (m317, step 6b, `FRING`, `buildCityRing`, `ringHouse`).**
  The kit city ended at its rectangle with empty grass round it. The island's ring (city edge to beach top) now
  holds the thin end of town, each row a BEARING (the rays' convention, in degrees) and `s`, a fraction across that
  ray's own grass (`isleRayAt`, `gw`) -- so a spot is always on the ring however wide it is there. Where the bridge
  comes in (bearing 28.6): a WAREHOUSE at 18 deg (26 x 14 x 6.5, a half-open roll-up door, a loading dock with crates,
  a forklift, and a 12-step outside stair to a flat roof you can walk) and a chain-link LOT at 39 deg with three
  parked cars; ten low HOUSES round the rest of the ring facing into the city with fenced back yards and a tree each;
  and ~40 TREES planted right against the city's edge every ~9 degrees (none within 5 deg of the bridge's line).
  **One identity frame** (`farmFrame(0, 0, 0)`: u = x, v = z) for the whole ring, so it is one mesh per material; a
  house is TURNED by psi = atan2(dx, dz) of its ray, its local +v out to sea and its front (-v) to the city, and every
  part goes through `L(lu, lv)` (the frame's own mapping) with `psi + p0`. 171 colliders.
  GOD `warehouse` (exempt from `places`' OFF THE FARMLAND: it is on the city's ring by design). That finishes step 6.

- **THE EDGE OF TOWN ON THE FARM'S SIDE OF THE RIVER (m316, step 6a, `FTOWN`, `buildTownEdge`, the `townedge` yard, per-yard owner codes).**
  "Never a line": between the fields and the bridge, a parcel (`FPLAN.yards` townedge, a superellipse 156 x 38 m
  either side of the landing, FENCED) holds a GAS STATION (canopy on four posts, two pump islands with lit screens,
  a shop with a lit window, an 11 m price sign -- exaggerated over a 3.5 m shop), a TRAILER PARK (four on blocks, a
  stripe, a deck, chairs, a dish), three small HOUSES with porches, picket-fenced yards, gates and mailboxes, two
  BILLBOARDS on 8 m legs (canvas boards, one facing traffic off the bridge, one onto it), a FRUIT STAND, POWER POLES
  every 30 m along the bridge road 5 m off it with wires sagging in three pieces, and the bridge road PAVED for its
  last stretch (a dark ribbon with a dashed centre line over the dirt track, fading into it).
  **Each yard is its own owner now** (`-2 - index`), so a yard chooses its border (`edge: 'fence'` for the town;
  the barn's and the house's stay hedged). The old `town_edge` reserve seed is gone -- the parcel replaced it, and
  the south wheat and plough shrank round it on their own. Everything else that reads owners only asks `< 0`.
  GOD `gas`, `trailers`. 6b (the city side starting thin, and the city island's own edge softened) follows.

- **THE FARMHANDS AND THE FARMER ARE AUTHORED NPC MARKERS, SO THE SHIPPED MARKER PATH SPAWNS THEM (m315, step 5c, `FHANDS`, `buildFarmhands`, `fpCentroid`).**
  Five people on the land: Dale in the wheat by the bridge road, Wendell on the west hill's hay, Mags in the orchard,
  Earl at the foot of the ploughed field watching the tractor, and Farmer Gristle at his barn doors (B2's farmer).
  **No new spawning code**: each row is pushed into `MARKS` as a `type: 'npc'` entry (`src: 'FARMHANDS'`) by
  `buildFarmhands`, which runs in the farm's build sequence -- BEFORE the crowd's deal (`kitPopulate` resets `K.at`)
  and `mkrNpcPlace` (checked: line 34120 against 34191). `mkrNpcPlace` deals it to its kind's `at`, the body spawns
  there, and `mkrStep` finds it within 2.5 m and gives it its home, its heading and its `lines` with the "!" -- STEER
  2's "speakers only from authored places", exactly the path his own `npc_*` markers take. Stand-ins per
  CHARACTERS.md: farmhands `hobo_01`, the farmer `hick_skinny` (`MKR.alias` farmer). They roam their kind's `roam`
  round the spot. A field row stands at its field's CENTROID off the owner lattice (`fpCentroid`) plus `off`, and is
  refused (`FARMHAND .. OFF FIELD`) if that lands outside the field.
  **What `npm run places` cannot see**: the bodies themselves (it loads no GLBs). It checks the five markers exist and
  stand on the farmland; whether each body spawned and talks is the phone's (GOD lists every talker as `TALK · name`).

- **A TRACTOR PLOUGHS AND A PICKUP RUNS THE BRIDGE ROAD (m314, step 5b, `FVEH`, `buildVehicles`, `vehStep`, `vehLanes`, `vehMerge`).**
  **The tractor** works the field under the far hill: `vehLanes` walks lines along the field's furrow `dir`, 5 m
  apart, takes the longest run whose lattice owner is the field (and 3 m either side of it), and trims 7 m into the
  headland -- 12 lanes, driven boustrophedon and ping-ponged, at 2.2 m/s, turning 0.55 rad/s, so the U-turns happen
  on the field and not through its fence. **The pickup** drives the lane's own centreline from the barn door (the
  lane's points put through the barn's frame) to its mouth, then `FPLAN`'s bridge road reversed to the bridge (its last
  point IS the lane's mouth, so the join is exact), waits 9 s, and comes back. Both are KINEMATIC followers (steer at
  the next waypoint at a capped turn rate, slow in the turns and near a waypoint), sit on `flHeightAt` and pitch to it
  (Euler order YXZ: yaw, then pitch about its own right; nose up = -atan(rise)), push him out of an oriented box along
  its shallower side, and stop (damped hard) if he is in the 5 m in front of them. Dust (`smokeAt`, earth colours)
  off the back while moving and within 140 m.
  **Each vehicle is ONE draw call**: `vehMerge` bakes its parts into a single vertex-coloured geometry (box, wheel and
  plough discs, the pickup's cab glass, lights and a bale in the bed). The parked tractor is still the barnyard's.
  **No engine sound** -- a held synth voice like the wreck's hum is the obvious next step. GOD `ploughing`, `pickup`
  (beside each, facing it, wherever it is). `npm run places` ticks `vehStep` with the rest.

  The m294 cows were six in the paddock and a field beside the old crash. On the farm's own land: the paddock keeps
  three, and `FHERDS` puts 27 more in six pastures (far hill 5, the neighbour's ridge 6, the slope above the creek
  mouth 5, the pond 4, home pasture 4, the creek pasture 3) -- 30, still ONE instanced draw (16 parts a cow), still
  redrawn only within 140 m. **A herd cow's home is its field's CENTROID off the owner lattice** (a seed is not the
  middle of its noise-bent cell) with a range from the field's own area, and `cowPick` only takes a spot whose lattice
  owner IS its field (`fpOwnAt`, a lookup, not `fpOwner` again) -- the pasture fences already stop a cow; this stops
  it choosing to walk into one and standing there stuck.
  `npm run places` now fails if any herd cow starts outside its own pasture. **Its first version read `bad` above
  that `let`'s own line** -- the repo's oldest landmine, in the checker this time: the count is carried past it.

- **THE NEIGHBOUR'S FARM ON THE RIDGE AND THE LONE HAY BARN (m312, step 4c, `FNEIGH`, `buildNeighbours`, `FARMLAND.FLATS`).**
  GAME_DESIGN's new "exaggerated scale and contrast" (tall and thin beside short and squat), on the ridge where the
  ridge track ends: a TALL, NARROW house (6 x 5.5, three lit floors, a 57-degree roof to 12.8 m, pale blue boards --
  not Gristle's cream), a LONG, SQUAT cattle shed (22 x 7, 2.9-3.4 m, open to the yard), a SKINNY water tower (12 m
  legs, a red tank, a cap, a ladder), and the FARM SHOP by the track (an awning, a counter, crates of apples, pumpkins
  and greens, a painted sign) where B1f's neighbour will stand. **The lone hay barn**: an open Dutch barn (ten steel
  posts, a curved roof) with its hay in three steps -- 1.5, 3.0, 4.5 m, each narrower -- climbable at `MOVE.jump`'s
  2.8 m, and 1 m of head room under the roof at the top step (the roof is at g + 7.3 over its 6 m-wide top block).
  **FLATS settle to their OWN ground's height**, not to the land's base: m306's yard flatten removes the hills (it sets
  `h` to 0), which on the RIDGE would have dug a pit into it. Each flat's height is measured at its middle with the
  flats off (`flatOn`), before the creek's bed and the pond's rim are sampled, then lerped in over r .5..1.
  **The curved roof** is a cylinder's top arc laid along u (`rotateZ(pi/2)`: (x, y, z) -> (-y, x, z), so its section is
  y' = R sin t, z' = R cos t, t in pi/2 +- .9) -- open-ended, so its material is DoubleSide or its inside is not drawn.
  **Caught before shipping**: the shop's awning slats tilted about the wrong axis (sideways): psi pi/2 and tilt -.25.
  The hay barn's footprint is a 15 m margin in `fpOwner` (no hay grows inside it). GOD `neighbour`, `haybarn`.

- **THE YARD IS TWO YARDS, THE HOUSE HAS ITS OWN, AND THE HEADLAND'S FIELDS STAND DOWN (m311, step 4b, `FPLAN.yards`, `FHOUSE.origin`, shed, coop, orchard).**
  The m306 parcel (one superellipse round everything m288-m305 built) is TWO small yards in `FPLAN.yards`: the
  BARNYARD where the barn, lean-to, silo, paddock and sunken lane always stood, and the HOUSEYARD 72 m north across the
  home pasture. **The farmhouse has its own frame** (`FHOUSE.origin`, th from `ub` - .12): its porch faces south to the
  barn, with a TOOL SHED (pent roof, a doorway, tools leaning, a drum) on one side and a CHICKEN COOP (a hut on legs,
  its ramp, a wire run) on the other. The ground the old parcel held is fields now (`home_corn` with the scarecrow
  moved into it, `home_pasture`, an `orchard` of small trees in rows, `creek_pasture`); a `home_track` runs barnyard
  to porch and the ridge and east tracks start from the house.
  **What stands down on the farm's own land**: `HROW` (the headland's hedgerow fields, plough, copse, bale stack --
  `FPLAN` does that job now), `FLORA.FIELDS` (the headland's crop rectangles -- `FCROP` plants `FPLAN`'s; the tufts
  stay), and the sunken lane's little BROOK with its culvert, ford and footbridge (the land has its creek valley).
  All three are gated on `FARMLAND.live`, not deleted. GOD lost `meadow`, `plough`, `copse` and `ford`; `corn`,
  `wheat` point at `FPLAN`'s fields, `orchard` is new.
  **Two caught before shipping**: the shed's pent roof was a rotation POST-MULTIPLIED onto a composed TRS (NOTES says
  that shears under a non-uniform scale; it is psi pi/2 with tilt -pt now, the porch roof's own trick); and GOD's
  `corn` landed exactly on its field's seed -- which is where the scarecrow now stands -- so on top of its post

- **THE FIELDS ARE AN AUTHORED PLAN, AND ONE RULE DRAWS THEM THREE TIMES (m308, step 3, `FPLAN`, `fpOwner`, `fpTint`, `buildFieldBounds`).**
  20 named SEEDS (crop + reason) and a superellipse PARCEL round m288-m305's cluster. A point of land belongs to the
  nearest seed, with the distance bent by per-seed value noise (`noise` 9 m) so borders wander instead of running as
  straight bisectors; **margins belong to no field** -- the beach, the creek's valley (9.5), the pond's bank (r + 11)
  and a 2.6 m strip either side of every TRACK, so a track is always the border it runs along and every boundary
  has a gap where a track crosses it. Measured: fields 2.2k-7.1k m2, the yard parcel 14.7k.
  **Use 1, the ground** (`aFld`, baked per land vertex in `buildFarmland`): rgb tints the grass (wheat gold, corn deep
  green, hay pale, ploughed brown), w = 10 + a furrow angle in the WORLD for a ploughed field, drawn as stripes in the
  land shader -- so the patchwork reads from the west hill before a single crop stands on it. The farmland got its
  own material (`isleLandMat({ fields, shareU })`) on the island's uniforms. **`m.defines = { FLD: 1 }` would have
  wiped MeshStandardMaterial's own `STANDARD` define** -- it is merged.
  **Use 2, the boundaries**: a 2 m owner lattice, a point wherever two owners meet, thinned to one per `piece` 2.7 m by
  a spatial hash, and each piece TURNED along its nearest same-pair neighbours either side (measured off the boundary,
  not assumed from the seeds -- the noise bends it). By the crops either side: hedge (bank, hedge collider, two
  clumps, an oak every `treeGap` 24), fence (post, two rails, one thin collider) where a pasture or a reserve is
  involved, a tree line (every `lineGap` 10) on a quarter of the crop pairs. 333 hedge, 303 fence, 95 trees.
  **(a, b) is a REFLECTION of (x, z)** (det[ua; ub] = -1): every ribbon here derives its winding off its first
  triangle, and the features frame takes (a, -b).
  **Use 3, the crops**: step 3b (not yet). **The tracks** are the lane's ribbon on the land's axes; `bridge_road` ends at
  the sunken lane's mouth, measured by putting the yard frame's (30, -9) through `buildFarm`'s placement
  (`fpLaneMouth`). The m305 fingerpost's TOWN arm now aims down it (it pointed down the m305 road, away from the bridge).
  GOD `swell`, `fplough`. Chip adds `h<hedges>f<fences>t<trees>` to `FL`.

- **THE CREEK VALLEY AND THE POND ARE CARVED INTO THE ONE HEIGHT FUNCTION (m307, step 2, `FARMLAND.CREEK`/`POND`, `flBase`, `buildFarmWaters`, `farmTree`).**
  `flHeight` is now `flBase` (m306's land) then two carves, so the mesh, the collider and the sea's depth all see the
  same valley and bowl. **The creek's bed is a RUNNING MINIMUM downstream** of (`flBase` - `dig`) sampled every 2 m and
  resampled to an even arc step (the per-segment sample counts round differently, so the raw array is not even) --
  its water can never run uphill or stand above the ground it is cut into. Measured: 5.19 at the source under the
  long ridge, -8.5 where it reaches the sea, 255 m long; where the land rises again (the low rise) it cuts a gorge.
  Profile: a slight channel `hb` 1.7 either side, then walls at `wall` .3 (17 deg, walkable).
  **The pond's level is MEASURED**: the lowest of 24 points on a ring 1.25 r out, minus .35 (and never under sea + .6),
  so its banks always hold it -- 0.1 here. Bowl `depth` 1.7, banks at `bank` .22 per metre.
  **Placed off a measurement of the m306 cluster in (a, b)** (`flLocal` over every farm box: a -99..56, b -60..18): the
  creek runs EAST of it (a 58..100), the pond WEST (a -140, b -75), the footbridge at point 2.35 east of the copse.
  **The water ribbon's first height floated**: +.22 over a bed whose channel lip is level with the bed put its edges
  .27 m over the bank; it is +.05 and `hb` + .25 wide now, so the edges dip into the walls.
  `farmTree` is the m303 tree lifted out of `buildHedgerows` (same `rr` draws in the same order, so the hedgerows'
  trees are unchanged) and takes any frame -- the pond's four willows use it. **The features frame**: `farmFrame` with
  th = atan2(-ua.z, ua.x) has u = a but v = -b (its v axis (sin th, cos th) is -ub), so everything goes in as (a, -b).
  Reeds in clumps round the pond with gaps (where the cows will drink), lily pads. GOD `creek`, `pond`.

  on bearing .5 rad (the sun's side, so from the farm the city is lit from behind you), `gap` 70 m of channel from
  the city island's waterline. Authored `HILLS` and `RIDGES`, each with its reason; the yard's patch settled level
  (`yard`, r 75) so m288-m305's pieces stand on it. **One height function** (`flHeight`) feeds the mesh, the collider
  (12,344 floor tris through `isleAppend`) and the water's depth; normals by central differences off it, so the nine
  chunks (`chunk` 40 cells of 5 m, culled by the camera) do not seam. The island's land material, shared.

  so it cannot carry a second shore. The farm has its own grid IN ITS OWN FRAME, depth = sea - max(`flHeight`,
  `isleBedAt`), on the sea's own uniforms (`wmat.clone()` with `uniforms` re-shared, `FARMW` defined); the city's water
  discards inside that turned rectangle (`uCut`, `uCutA`). **First cut was an axis-aligned box round the turned
  island: it reached back to x -14, over the city's own coast, and drew 23,810 water tris -- the turned rect is 8,254.**

- **THE FARM HAD NOBODY'S HOUSE (m304, farm pass 9, `FHOUSE`, `buildFarmhouse`, `farmhouseStep`).**
  REGIONS.md: *"the farmer and his family"* -- and the yard was a barn, a silo and a lean-to. Pass 9 is the farmhouse,
  the biggest silhouette that was missing: two storeys of cream board-and-batten (`cream`, FPAINT kind 1) on a stone
  plinth, an oxide-red roof with the ridge along the porch, a stone chimney on the +u gable, every window LIT (`glow`,
  emissive 0xffc56a), green shutters, a deep porch facing the corn and the lane with chairs and a table and steps down
  the middle. **Vertical**: a rain barrel (1.05) beside the porch's east end, then the porch roof (~3 m, walkable
  `quad`) -- one jump each at `MOVE.jump` 10.6 / g 20 (2.8 m). **Alive**: chimney smoke (`smokeAt`, within 160 m) and a
  washing line behind the house, four sheets on ONE `InstancedMesh` swinging in `farmhouseStep`.
  **WHERE, MEASURED NOT GUESSED**: u 9.5..18.5, v 7.5..14.5 -- the one empty plot in the yard on m303's frame map,
  between the corn (v <= 2), the hay meadow (v >= 18.5), the paddock fence (u <= 6) and the yard's east hedge (u ~21).
  **Orientation, checked by hand** (the m288 fence rule): with psi = pi/2 a box's local x points -v, so a roof slab on
  the +v side rises toward the ridge with tilt +ang (the barn's is -s ang because its local x is +u), and the porch
  roof, higher at the wall (+v), takes -tl. The gables are the barn's extrude turned Ry(pi/2): shape x -> -v
  (symmetric), extrusion z -> +u, so they straddle the end walls. The cloth's Euler is 'YXZ' (Ry psi puts the sheet's
  width along the line, then Rx swings it about the line) in the frame group's own local space.
  **Caught on the read-back before shipping**: a step formula that multiplied its own height by 0, front rails that ran
  0.35 m past the porch's end post, a log-pile collider 0.65 m taller than its logs, and GOD's spot in the corn.
  GOD `farmhouse` (on the path, facing the porch). Ground paint `porch` (the worn path). Chip `FH<boxes+tris>`.

  drawn to ~31, so "the wheat down to the shore" stopped 24 m short. At 24 the farm's ray has 65.6 m (`need` 60).
  **(2) what is left is fields**: four hedgerow RUNS (bank .5 + hedge 1.45, over a man; leaf clumps on a collider; a
  piece on beach ground is skipped, so every hedge stops at the shore by itself), a tree standing IN each run every
  ~13 m, a gate in each (two posts and a five-bar gate swung open), a copse of nine oaks at the headland's tip, three
  willows on the river bank, the PLOUGHED field as one ribbon of ridges down the slope (20 cm, drawn not collided --
  under a step), round bales in the hay meadow and a stack of three to climb. Crops are rows in `FLORA.FIELDS` (hay,
  stubble, potatoes on the ridge tops via `jit`/`lift`, rough grass, ferns) -- no new draw call. After: **15% of the
  GRASS is bare** (grass only, not beach; the 56% counted beach too, so the two are not the same measure).
  **The creek and the wheat now reach the beach** (the creek was a fixed 40 m polyline that stopped mid-field; it

  every instance; +3 m for the sway.

  swung by psi - 1.22 opens toward the run's left; the bale stack's axes are perpendicular to its offset (dot 0); the

  STEER: *"THE FARM DOES NOT EXIST IN THE REAL GAME. Colin opened every GOD place and none of them work."* `npm run
  places` (the planning session's new tool: the REAL kit collider and island, every farm builder, then the shipped
  `godPlace`) read the widest grass as 14.9 m against `buildFarm`'s 18, so `FARM NO ROOM 15` and `FARM.at` null --
  and crash, lane, bridge, cows, flora, props and ground paint all return early on that null, so **m288 to m301 were
  never in his game.** Every one of them was checked by reading code against a farm frame nobody had built.
  **AND THE 14.9 WAS A SAMPLE INDEX, NOT A COAST.** `isleSamples` gives segment i the NEXT control point's count
  (`P[i + 1][5]`), so the beach top is sample 1 + 10 + 5 = **16**; `ISLE_J0` was typed 12 off a comment that counted
  "1 + 1 + 10". Sample 12 is a fifth of the way across the grass: every reader got 2 + (grass - 2) / 5. The ring's real
  grass is 38 to 66 m on the sides. The water grid also started at 12, under the land (hidden, never wrong to look at).
  Fixed to 16, **checked at build against the profile it names** (`ISLE J0 a/b` in the chip if they ever disagree), and
  a ray now carries `gw` (grass) and `L` outright so nothing counts samples to ask.
  **THE FARM STILL GOT ITS OWN GROUND, AS THE STEER SAID.** "The widest ray" is not an authored place, and the layout
  needs ~60 m city-edge-to-beach (lane's town bank at v -24 with 3 m to the city; wheat to v +31 with shore past it --
  `FARM.need` 60, derived from those two, replacing the guessed 18). `ISLE.head` is Gristle Farm's headland: a lobe on
  the waterline at bearing .12 rad (the +x side, under the low sun, so the yard's shadows fall back toward town),
  `out` 34 m over a flat middle of +-.375 rad easing to 0 at +-.75, the wobble calmed .65 under it. **Only in `tkit`**:
  the toon city has no farm and an empty lobe would be empty ground. `buildFarm` stands on the ray nearest `head.th`.

  ok  wheat      -> player 142.7,-1.0,22.0 ground -1.17 
  ok  windmill   -> player 131.5,-0.7,17.4 ground -0.86 
  ok  scarecrow  -> player 117.4,-0.2,2.9 ground -0.38

  every tkit GOD place is somewhere
  ok  farmPropsStep  30 frames

- **THE GROUND PAINT SITS ON `triGround`, AND A RIBBON'S WINDING DECIDES WHETHER IT EXISTS (m301, farm pass 7, `GPAINT`, `buildGroundPaint`).**
  One transparent MeshStandard overlay with RGBA vertex colours (three turns on `vertexAlphas` for a 4-wide colour
  attribute): grid patches from `GPAINT.TABLE` with alpha falling off by a noise-wobbled elliptic radius, and the lane's
  floor as a ribbon (`LANE.pts`, stored by `buildLane`) with two darker rut lines. **Heights come from
  `triGround(x, z, 1.5, 0)`, not `groundAt`** -- the latter answers a box top where a patch crosses a bank or the barn
  plinth and stretches triangles up its face; capped at 1.5 m, the terrain floor is all `triGround` can see (roofs are
  above it). **Winding, checked by hand:** a grid of (u, v) with indices (o, o+row, o+1) faces up; the ribbon indexed
  (along, across) the same way faced DOWN (along x across, with across = along turned +90 deg, points to -y), so
  FrontSide would have culled the whole lane track -- it is wound (o, o+1, o2) now.

- **THE WRECK'S GLOW IS FAKED ON THE GROUND, NOT LIT (m300, farm pass 6, `CHERO`, `crashHero`, `crashHeroStep`).**
  A `PointLight` would light the field for real and would cost every lit fragment in the city a light loop (and
  recompile every material when it is added). The pool is an additive radial-gradient texture on a 16x16 grid whose
  vertices sit at `groundAt + .07`, so it hugs the slope instead of cutting into it; it pulses with the core. The beam is
  an open cone with vertex colours fading to black at the top (additive black is invisible), `fog: false` because a
  fogged ADDITIVE surface adds the fog colour and glows white in the haze. The core's own emissive is the crash
  material `MAT.glow`, kept on `CRASH.glowMat`; the heartbeat is `sin^6`, with a 2% stutter. Arcs are `spkBurst` + the
  `zap` sample, only within 90 m. The hum is ONE held voice (two saws at 55 Hz +- cents and a 110 Hz saw, lowpass 240,
  6.5 Hz tremolo on a gain node) created inside `humOut` and stopped outside it, counted in `SFX.voices` once.
  The ten scorch discs went through `farmMerge` (10 draws -> 1). Debris is its own `farmFrame` ('wreckbits'), painted.
  `CRASH.frame` hands the crash's own frame numbers to the hero pass. Chip `CR..a<arcs>h` (h while the hum plays).

- **A TILTED STRUT IS ITS OWN GEOMETRY UNDER AN EULER, NOT A ROTATION MULTIPLIED ONTO A TRS (m299, farm pass 5, `FPROPS`, `buildFarmProps`).**
  I wrote the windmill's legs the m291 way first -- `bx()` then `matrix.multiply(makeRotationZ(...))` -- which rotates
  BEFORE the non-uniform scale and shears the box; caught on re-reading. A leg is `BoxGeometry(.12, L, .12)` at the
  midpoint with Euler `(rx, 0, rz)`: XYZ order applies Rz first, so `rz = -asin(dx/L)` puts the y axis's x component at
  dx/L and then `rx = asin(dz/(L cos rz))` its z (y comes out H/L by construction). The tractor first had `psi = pi/2`,
  which in this frame runs a box's first dimension along -v -- 90 deg off its own wheels; a box's FIRST dimension runs
  along `(cos psi, -sin psi)` in (u, v). The weathervane's arrowhead points INTO the wind (its fin streams down it): yaw =
  downwind + pi. The wind is one direction for the yard -- `FPROPS.wind` [.8, .6], the same vector `FLORA`'s shader leans
  the crops along -- turned into the farm frame with the frame's inverse. Props are built right after `buildFarm`, before
  the cows and plants, so `cowClear` and the tuft rule see their colliders. `FARM.barn` carries the barn's numbers.

- **GOD MODE IS ONE KEY THAT NEVER FOLDS, AND FLY REPLACES `stepPlayer` (m298, STEER, `GOD`, `GODPLACES`, `godTo`, `godFlyStep`).**
  *"Colin can't see anything you've built."* The world/collider/fx keys are `display: none` under `body.chipmin`, and
  the chip folds BY DEFAULT (m148) -- so a key added "with the world key" would have been invisible on every cold start.
  `#godKey` is excluded from that rule and moves to `--gut` when folded, `--gut4` (new, `hudGutter`) when open.
  **Fly is `if (GOD.fly) godFlyStep(dt); else stepPlayer(dt);`** -- not a velocity fight with the physics -- moving
  through `stickWorld()` (the walk's own bearing) at `flyV`, rising/sinking by the two `.godfb` keys or space/C. The sea
  and river rules skip while flying. **`godTo` moves the camera by the same delta** (`portalGo`'s rule) and clears
  `river.safe`. A place in another world sets `sessionStorage` world + `mel.godGo` and reloads; `godBoot` (first
  `godStep` after `rig.ready`) jumps there -- after `crashSpawn`, so a fresh save still lands on the place. Safety is
  early returns at the TOP of `playerHurt`, `heatAdd`, `juicePay`, plus `HEAT.v = 0` per step. The DNA mode comes back
  by rebuilding the mode row from `WEAP.modesAll` (saved before the m282 filter). The form wheel lists `godForms()`
  and `formKind` now also resolves any LOADED roster kind. Map tap: the inverse of `mapU`/`mapV`, onto
  `groundAt(x, z, 300, 400)` (the highest surface). **The page is `touch-action: none` from the root**, so the menu
  drags its own `scrollTop` and its buttons fire on pointerUP only when the finger did not move 7 px.
  **Standing rule (STEER): everything built must be reachable from GOD in the same build** -- a place is one line in
  `GODPLACES`.

- **THE FARM'S PLANTS BEND IN WORLD UNITS, AFTER THE INSTANCE MATRIX (m297, farm pass 4, `FLORA`, `buildFlora`, `floraMat`).**
  One `InstancedMesh` of a 7-blade fan (height 1, vertex colour dark root -> light tip), scaled per instance into corn,
  wheat or a tuft, coloured per instance. `project_vertex` is re-written so the wind and his wake are added AFTER
  `instanceMatrix`: displacement in world xz, times `position.y^2` (root planted) and the instance's own height
  (`length(instanceMatrix[1].xyz)`), so a stalk bows further than a tuft. Bending in LOCAL space would have been divided
  by each instance's non-uniform scale and turned by its random yaw. `worldpos_vertex` (shadow receiving) does not see
  the bend -- received shadows are a few cm off on a bowing stalk, accepted. No shadows CAST. Placement: the fields are
  `FLORA.FIELDS` (named patch in the farm frame + `why`), rejected per stalk off the beach and out of boxes; tufts are
  the RULE "within `tuftR[1]` of a box, not within `tuftR[0]`" via two `resolveBoxes` probes. Built last in the farm
  sequence so every wall exists. The shader was compiled on instanced test geometry with shadows and fog before
  shipping (2 programs, 0 errors). Chip `FL<plants>`.

- **THE FARM IS PAINTED IN THE SHADER, PER KIND, AND THE GLSL WAS COMPILED BEFORE IT SHIPPED (m296, farm pass 3, `FPAINT`, `farmPaint`).**
  `farmFrame` calls `farmPaint(MAT[k], k)` on every material it is handed, so the farm, crash, lane and bridge all get
  it; the cows (one instanced mesh) do not. The patch adds `vFpP`/`vFpN` (world position and normal, from
  `transformed`/`objectNormal` after `begin_vertex`) and rewrites `diffuseColor.rgb` after `color_fragment`: kind 1
  boards (seams every 1/4.6 m on the dominant non-top axis, a hash tint per board, wear to grey wood by noise), 2
  stone (.7 x .34 m courses, offset rows, lighter mortar), 3 roof (seams every .45 m, rust), 4 hay, 5 earth, 6 leaf,
  7 metal, 0 variation only. `FP_KIND` is a define and `customProgramCacheKey` is `fpaint<kind>`, so one program per
  kind. **A shader that fails to compile does not blank the page, it makes the farm vanish** -- so the shipped text
  (lifted from index.html between `const FPAINT` and `farmFrame`) was rendered on a cube per kind in headless Chromium
  + SwiftShader with fog and shadows on: 10 programs, 0 errors. A string `.replace` that finds no chunk fails SILENTLY
  (no paint, no error) -- if a three upgrade renames `color_fragment` or `begin_vertex`, this goes flat without a word.

- **THE FARM'S GOLDEN HOUR IS A GRADE BLENDED BY DISTANCE, WITH ONE PER-FRAME WRITER (m295, farm pass 2, `GRADE`, `gradeStep`).**
  REGIONS.md's "late golden hour". `gradeStep` (after `stepSun`) owns `sun.color`, `hemi.color`, `hemi.groundColor`,
  `scene.fog.near/far` per frame, lerping from bases it captured on its first run toward gold by
  `k = damp(1 - smooth(50, 90, dist to FARM.at), .9 s)`, fading over the first 14 m inside `ISLE.rect`. Nothing else
  writes those colours after construction (grepped); `flatSet` writes INTENSITIES, which the grade leaves alone. The
  fog colour's base is the sky bake's (`skyApply` stores `GRADE.fog0` when it writes), so a re-bake moves the base.
  **`GRADE` is declared above `SKY`** because `skyApply` runs at module scope (`skyBake()` at load) and touches it.
  When k settles to 0 it writes the bases once (`k0`) and then stops writing. The sun DIRECTION is not graded:
  `sunSet` re-bakes the sky. **A screenshot tool was tried and dropped**: headless Chromium + SwiftShader boots the kit
  city in ~20 s but `page.screenshot` times out (30 s) waiting for one frame -- the city is too heavy for software GL.

- **HIS MARKERS ARE READ IN `side()`, BEFORE THE BUILDER, AND MY FIRST TWO NAMES WERE TAKEN (m293, STEER 3, `MKR`, `MARKS`, `mkrRead`, `mkrApply`).**
  `buildTCity` merges and prunes 19,814 nodes, and an empty pruned is a marker lost, so `mkrRead(g.scene)` runs inside
  `side()` before `tag.build(g)` for KCITYVIS / KCITYCOL / KCITYBLD / TOONBRK. The kit-city GLBs sit at identity, so
  `matrixWorld` after `updateMatrixWorld(true)` on the unparented scene IS the world. **`MARK` (the melee target ring,
  m51) and `markStep` already existed** -- the syntax gate caught both as redeclarations, which in the shipped file
  would each have been a BLANK PAGE. Mine are `MKR` / `mkr*`. Grep a name before declaring it; this file has 31,000
  lines and every short word is taken.
  Order: `mkrApply` (portals, gates, regions) after the world's builders; `mkrNpcPlace` AFTER `kitPopulate`, because
  `crowdDeal` resets every kind's `K.at` -- an npc marker is one more entry in its kind's `at`, spawned by the kind's
  own builder; `mkrStep` then finds that body (nearest of the kind within 2.5 m, not yet claimed) and gives it the role
  (home = the marker, facing, talk). `mkrSpawn` runs before `crashSpawn` and replaces it when a `spawn_start` exists.
  Facing: glTF +Z = Blender -Y; `yaw_deg` overrides. Measured his three files: none of the new types yet; the buildings
  file holds `police_stand` x60, `police_spawn`, `police_car_park`, `firemen_spawn`, `fire_truck_home`, `door_in/out`
  x118, `ladder_bottom` x120 that no code reads. STEER 2's dormancy: `TALK.seed` 0, q0 `dormant` (`qon:<id>` flag).

- **SYSTEMS SHIP DORMANT; NOTHING IS PLACED "NEAR THE SPAWN" (m292, STEER 1, `GATE.demo`, `PORTAL.demo`).** *"Placeholders are
  being dropped in at random and it looks sloppy."* m285/m286 put two demo gates and three demo portal pads round
  wherever he spawned, on open ground found by `spawnBeside`, with no reason to be there -- and from m289 that meant
  round the farm. Both flags are 0; `gateDemo(force)` / `portalDemo(force)` keep the placement for `mel.gateDemo()` /
  `mel.portalDemo()`. **The rule now**: a thing enters the world from a named Blender marker or an authored placement
  table entry with a named spot and a reason -- never from a search for somewhere open. **The m292 cows were built before
  the STEER arrived and were NOT shipped** (STEER 4 pauses the farm): they live on `paused/cows-m292`. Main's m292 is
  this build; the branch's m292 never deployed.
- **THE HERD IS ONE `InstancedMesh` OF ONE UNIT BOX, AND THE MOO IS A SYNTH (m294, ROADMAP B1d2 -- built at m292, parked by the STEER, returned as farm pass 1, `COW`, `COWS`, `cowStep`, `cowDraw`, `mooAt`).**
  Sixteen instances a cow (body, udder, three coat bands, four legs, tail, head, muzzle, two ears, two horns), each matrix
  `root * T(pivot) * Ry * Rx * Rz * T(centre) * S(size)` composed per frame in `cowPut`; colours set once with
  `setColorAt`. One draw call for six cows; `frustumCulled = false` because an InstancedMesh's bounding sphere is its
  geometry's, not its instances'. A patchless coat draws its bands at scale 0 (degenerate, no fragments).
  The head pivot is the neck: positive `Rx` tips the forward end DOWN (Rx maps z to `(0, -sin a, cos a)`), and grazing
  also lowers the neck .35 m -- worked through by hand, the muzzle lands .1-.3 m over the grass at pitch 1.05.
  Brains: graze / look / walk / trot. A spot is clear by `cowClear` (grass above sea + .5, outside `ISLE.rect` + 2,
  outside the river channel via the bridge's inverse frame, and a 1.1 m `resolveBoxes` probe touching nothing) -- so every
  wall, fence, hedgebank and levee is already a fence for them. Walking pushes through `resolveBoxes` at r .75 and climbs
  only `COW.step` .32, so the bale stair and the banks stop them; boxes under `MOVE.step` (furrow berms) are walked
  through, a known clip. **`cowStep` runs after `gatePush`, before the camera**, because it shoves the player (two circles
  along the body). The moo (`mooAt`): two saws +-7 cents and a square sub an octave down, lowpass 260 -> 980 -> 620 ->
  280 Hz x k, a +7 dB peak at 520 x k, pitch .82 -> 1.06 -> .98 -> .72 of `f0` 112 x k, 5.2 Hz vibrato; faded with
  `smooth(mooFull, mooOut, d)` like `snd`, panned by the camera's world-matrix right vector; counts one `SFX.voices`.
  Chip `COW6m<moos>s<startles>`; `m0` for a minute next to them means no audio context yet (nothing has been touched).

- **THE BRIDGE BROUGHT ITS OWN RIVER, AND THE RAMPS ARE UNTURNED BOXES (m291, ROADMAP B1d, `BRIDGE`, `buildBridge`, `riverStep`).**
  The island has no river, so the farm gets one: two stone levees (3 m) from an outfall headwall at the city's edge to the
  beach, water ribbon between, and `riverStep` -- inverse farm frame (`u = dx C - dz S`, `v = dx S + dz C`, times the
  mirror `BRIDGE.side`) -- puts him back on the last grounded spot outside the channel when he is in it below the levee
  top - 1.2. Its own safe spot, not `ISLE.safe`, because the island would happily save one in the river bed.
  **Placement is measured**: at the river's u, `ve` walks v out of `ISLE.rect` and `vb` walks on to the beach top; under
  30 m of grass and the whole layout mirrors (`U(u) = sg * u`). **The fence rule (`psi = atan2(-dv, du)`, local x along
  the travel) is for things whose FIRST dimension is their length**; a ramp's first dimension is its width, so the first
  version would have laid every ramp sideways. All ramps run along v, so their boxes are unturned (w across u, step
  length along v) and the road plank tilts by `rx = -atan2(rise per +v, L)` (Rx maps local z to `(0, -sin a, cos a)`).
  **Never post-multiply a composed TRS matrix by a rotation** -- it rotates before the scale and shears the box; the first
  plank did. The hairpin: A (field -> landing, toward town), the landing, B (landing -> abutment, seaward), the deck on
  the levees, C (far abutment -> down toward town). Ramps are `quad` floors over stepped earth boxes (top just under the
  floor) with parapets, so there is no way underneath. Checkpoint: booth on the east levee cap, barrier arm across the
  deck, `BRIDGE.gate = { x, z, y, h, w }` for B2's cordon. Chip `BR<boxes>/<tris>` and `~<put-backs>`.

- **THE HOLLOWAY IS SUNK BY ITS BANKS, NOT DUG (m290, ROADMAP B1c, `LANE`, `buildLane`, `banks()`).**
  The island's ground is one ray-grown mesh whose floors live in `TRI`/`SURF`; a trench would be a rebuild of the coast.
  So the lane stays at field level between 1.9 m earth banks (inner half a walkable path, outer half a hedge collider
  with icosahedron clumps drawn over it), and the creek runs between 1.25 m stone-faced banks with a water ribbon at
  ground + .1. **Bank side is by NORMAL, not by v**: the lane runs toward -u, so `sd = +1` is the town side; the first
  version opened gaps by an absolute v, which would have opened both banks the moment `laneOut` pushed the lane outward.
  `laneOut` walks every lane point out (+v) until its town bank is 3 m clear of `ISLE.rect` -- the farm frame is skewed
  off its ray, so the city edge is not at one v. The creek's source is walked out the same way. The ford is where the
  creek meets the lane (both bank pairs skipped by distance from it); the footbridge is a deck at bank-top height on the
  town-side bank line, spanning the ford, with railing colliders. One `farmFrame` commit (tag `lane`). Chip `LN<boxes>`.

- **A NEW GAME WAKES AT THE WRECK, AND THE MOVE HAPPENS AFTER `kitPopulate` (m289, ROADMAP B1b, `CRASH`, `buildCrash`, `crashSpawn`, `farmFrame`).**
  `kitPopulate` drops the crowd round `player.pos` and puts Clancy beside it, so moving the player first would have moved
  Old Town's people onto the farm. `crashSpawn` runs right after it (crowd stays in town), overwrites `CLANCY.at` with
  the wreck's hatch, and comes before the spawn's height is taken. It fires while `SAVE.ch === 0 && !flags.inTown`;
  `crashStep` sets `inTown` the first time he is 4 m inside `ISLE.rect`. `?spawn=city|crash` overrules it.
  **`farmFrame` is m288's helpers lifted out** (turned boxes, merged meshes, floor quads, one commit); the farm and the
  crash both use it. **Three sign/order traps, all caught by hand before shipping:** (1) yaw for "local x along the
  furrow" is `+fpsi` with `fpsi = atan2(-dv, du)` (the fence rule), not `-fpsi`; (2) three's default Euler order is XYZ,
  so the matrix is Rx*Ry*Rz and Rz (the tip) is applied FIRST -- right for tip-then-yaw, wrong for a torus that must be
  laid flat first, so the rim's lay-flat is baked into its geometry (`rotateX`); (3) a world-space flat ellipse turned
  `g` about z then laid flat by Rx(-pi/2) has its long axis at `(-sin g, -cos g)`. The fire is a real `fireStart`
  ground fire with `life: Infinity`, re-lit every 4 s if the pool's eviction (oldest non-room fire at `FIRE.max`) took
  it. Smoke is `smokeAt` k 6, dark, ~3/s. Chip: `CR<boxes>` and `*` when this boot woke there.

- **THE FARM IS BUILT IN A TURNED FRAME, AND THE OBB CONVENTION IS `cs = cos t, sn = -sin t` FOR A MESH TURNED `t` (m288, ROADMAP B1a, `buildFarm`, `farmMerge`).**
  `boxNear`/`resolveBoxes` read an oriented box's local x as `(cs, sn)` in the world; a THREE mesh turned `t` about +Y
  has its local x at `(cos t, -sin t)` -- so `sn = -sin t`, which is the toon city's `yaw = -t` written out. **m287's
  map drew every oriented box mirrored** (both corner offsets had the wrong sign); fixed here, from the same algebra.
  Placement is the widest grass on the ring: `ISLE.rays[i].smp[ISLE_J0][0]` is that ray's grass (sample 12 is the beach
  top). Local frame: u along the tangent, v out to sea, `wx/wz` and the group's own rotation agree (local x -> `(C, -S)`).
  **A box turned `psi` in that frame runs along `(cos psi, -sin psi)` in (u, v)** -- the first fence used
  `atan2(du, dv) - pi/2` and got the sign of v backwards; it is `atan2(-dv, du)` now. Roofs are floor quads offered in
  both windings to `isleAppend` (which re-pushes `TRI.v`/`SURF.v` and rebuilds; `triBuild` empties its raw list, so
  appending without that would delete the city's floors). Colliders go into `BOXES`, then one `boxGrid()`. Every piece
  is merged per material (`farmMerge`, ~8 draws). The bale stair is .45 a step (MOVE.step is .5 x SZ) ending exactly at
  the loft's edge. Known: roof triangles are floors only, so a jump from the loft can come up through the roof near the
  eaves, and the barn's overhang clips a player walking the lean-to right against the wall. Chip: `FARM<boxes>/<tris>`;
  `FARM FAIL` / `FARM NO ROOM` in the missing list if it could not build.

- **THE MAP IS THE COLLIDER DRAWN FLAT, AND ITS ROTATION COMES FROM THE CAMERA'S OWN DIRECTION (m287, ROADMAP A9, `MAP`, `mapBuild`, `mapMini`).**
  No minimap existed though the roadmap said "tap the minimap". A top-down render into a target was the obvious
  picture and it would have fought `cellStep` (far cells hidden), the x-ray dither, the fog and the sky -- so the base
  is every `BOXES` footprint (oriented ones turned by `cs/sn/hx/hz`) onto a 1024 2D canvas, sorted by `maxy`, shaded by
  height; slabs over 300 m are skipped as ground. **Screen right is -X** (+X is his left): `mapU = -(x-cx)*s`,
  `mapV = -(z-cz)*s`. The minimap's turn is `-pi/2 - atan2(-fz, -fx)` off `camera.getWorldDirection` -- derived from
  the lens itself so `cam.az`'s convention never enters it; his arrow is `-h` (checked: forward `(sin h, cos h)` lands at
  canvas `(-sin h, -cos h)`). Rebuilt when the box count drifts (checked every 8 s) and on opening. Regions default to
  extent quadrants keyed `<world>:<id>` in `SAVE.regions`; `MAPREG[world]` overrides. Fog is a second canvas, redrawn
  only on a reveal. Minimap 15 Hz, full map 5 Hz while open. Chip: `RG<seen>/<regions>b<builds>`.

- **A PORTAL TRIP MOVES THE CAMERA BY THE SAME DELTA AS HIM (m286, ROADMAP A8b, `PORTALS`, `portalGo`, `portalTap`).**
  `mel.brk()` teleports by setting `p.pos` alone and the lens swoops after him; `portalGo` adds the same delta to
  `cam.pos` and `cam.tgt`, so it arrives framed as it left. Activation is contact (`r` flat, 1.2 m in y) ->
  `progPortal(id)`; ids are `<world>_<name>` so pads in different worlds never share a save key. The right tap order
  is `talkTap` -> `portalTap` -> wings -> jump; `E` on desktop does talk-or-travel. The hub (`hub: 1`) is active from
  the start (and written to the save) so the first pad found already has a destination. Demo pads go down 1.6 s
  after `rig.ready` through `spawnBeside`, avoiding the gates. Chip: `PT<active>/<placed>>trips`.

- **A GATE IS ITS OWN PUSH, NOT A BOX IN `BOXES` (m285, ROADMAP A8, `GATE_TYPES`, `gatePush`, `gateAdd`).**
  A box in `BOXES` blocks everyone always and that list is a spatial index built at load; a gate blocks one body
  sometimes. `gatePush` runs after the player moves and before `kitCamStep`/`stepCam`, in the gate's frame (normal is
  `(sin h, cos h)`, `v` along it, `u` along the gate): inside the slab by `p.r`, in the wrong form, he is put back on
  `G.side` (the side he was last on, so a fast frame cannot tunnel) and the velocity into it is removed. Blocks up to
  `GATE.hi` above its base, so a jump does not clear a cordon. Crossing in the right form sets `gate:<id>` (A3's
  step); a `fix` gate sets it when mended. Needs are FORM NAMES compared with `formNow()`; `gap` needs `glider`, which
  no file is called yet. Two demo gates go down 1.5 s after `rig.ready` via `spawnBeside` (Clancy's search), not in
  Weirdport. Visuals are primitives (posts and tape, additive cones, planks), placeholders until he models them.
  Bodies ignore gates. Toast (`toast()`) is the one-line message low in the middle; chip `G<placed>/<stops>`.

- **THE TRANSFORM IS PAID FOR INSIDE `morphGo`, SO NO PATH TO A FORM SKIPS IT (m284, ROADMAP A7b, `JUICE`, `juicePay`, `juiceStep`).**
  The sampler, the form wheel, the DNA gun and `mel.dna` all end in `morphGo(K)`; `juicePay()` sits after its own
  refusals (busy, not wearable, already that) and before the state is touched, and refuses with a `NO JUICE` card.
  `morphOff` (K null) is free. Drain runs in `juiceStep` only while `p.mphK && !p.mphSt` and calls `morphOff()` at zero.
  **`SAVE.juice` changes every frame while worn, so it is saved on a `saveT` clock**, plus on every gain/cost -- a
  per-frame `localStorage.setItem` is a stall on a phone. New game: `juiceInit` flag fills the tank once (progReset
  clears flags, so a reset refills). Skinsuit reward is the edge into `down` on a `wasK` body (`d.jDn`), the same
  edge trick as the quest's `d.qDn`. Rates on the tune panel, top section JUICE. Chip: `J<juice>` and `!<snap-backs>`.

- **THE FORM WHEEL IS ONE BUTTON AND A PICKER, NOT A RING OF FORMS (m283, ROADMAP A7, `FORMS`, `formKind`, `formNow`).**
  A third left ring with one segment per form is 30 px a segment past four forms, so `#formRow` is a single `FORMS`
  segment at r 148-178, span 30 about straight up (left tip 48 px in on a 390 px phone, pad centre 94 px in), built by
  the same `buildArcRow`, and it opens `#formPick` -- round buttons on a circle, z-index 9 over the zones, tap outside
  to close, no pause. A saved form is a NAME; `formKind` resolves it per world from `FORMK`, then any `DUMMIES` body of
  that kind, then `she`, and caches into `FORMK`. `undefined` = not loaded here (greyed), `null` = zap. `formNow()` is
  the current form's name, for A8's gates. Row painting writes `sel` only on open/close and on/off changes.

- **THE DNA ROW IS FILTERED BEFORE `buildArcRow`, NOT BESIDE THE SAMPLER (m282, ROADMAP A6, `SAMPLE`, `sampleStep`, `cardShow`).**
  My first version filtered `WEAP.modes` inside the sampler block, ~15,000 lines below `buildArcRow(modeRow,
  WEAP.modes, ...)`, which runs at module scope -- the segment would have been drawn from the old list for a mode that
  no longer existed. It is filtered right above that call now, off its own `?dna` regex (a `SAMPLE.gun` read there
  would be a TDZ blank page). `modeNow()` indexes `WEAP.modes[WEAP.mode]` so the shorter list is safe.
  The gesture is the backflip duck's own "held at rest" test (`R.far < MOVE.tapR`); `samp.near` joins the duck's busy
  list so the two never share a hold. **The downed body's lie clock is CLAMPED while the thumb is down** (an officer's
  `out` is 1.4 s, shorter than `hold`) -- a clamp, never a set, and only while held. A sample is `progForm` (saved) +
  `morphGo` (worn now). `FORMK` maps names to kind tables for this session only -- A7 must resolve saved names to
  tables on a fresh load (the kinds are all in `CIVILS` + the named tables). The quest card is `cardShow` now, shared.

- **THE COP'S AIM IS `shoot_pistol` HELD ON ITS CLAMPED LAST FRAME (m281, ROADMAP A5b, `copFire`, `copExtras`, `copTracer`).**
  Every non-loop clip on a body is `LoopOnce` + `clampWhenFinished` and is `play()`ed at spawn at weight 0, so it
  has already run out and holds its end pose; giving `shoot_pistol` weight 1 between rounds therefore holds the aim,
  and `skinPlay` rewinds it per round. `draw_weapon` plays once per drawing (`d.gun`, cleared below 3 stars). The round
  leaves `fireLag` after the shoot starts (`d.shotAt`), and only when he faces you within .35 rad. Hit chance is a
  linear `acc` over `shootR`, divided by `1 + speed/accRun`; `p.roll` always misses. Muzzle is a typed offset off the
  root (no hand bone looked up) -- the tracer start is approximate.
  **REINFORCEMENTS ARE SPAWNED AND REMOVED IN `heatStep`, NOT IN `copAI`** -- `heatStep` runs before `stepDummies`
  walks `DUMMIES`, and splicing that list mid-walk skips the next body (`VTURN`, m162). They need `DUMMY.P`, so a world
  with no officer loaded gets none. Spot: behind you, `extraR` out, through `kitStand` in the kit worlds or
  `groundAt` + `resolveBoxes` elsewhere. Chip adds `sh<hits>/<shots>` and `+<extras>`.

- **THE OFFICER HAD WALK AND RUN CLIPS ALL ALONG AND NOBODY NAMED THEM (m280, ROADMAP A5a, `COPS`, `copAI`, `heatStep`).**
  `dummy_officer.glb` carries `walk_01 run_01 run_02 draw_weapon shoot_pistol hit_while_shooting` besides the idle,
  hits, falls and get-ups `DUMMY.clips` used -- read straight out of the JSON chunk, the m67 lesson again: read the
  export before deciding what is missing. m280 names walk/run and gives `DUMMY` `cop: 1`; `copAI` sits in
  `stepDummies`' free branch ABOVE `K.ai`, so every hit, fall and get-up still outranks the chase. Gait refs are
  GUESSED (1.35 / 3.8) -- `npm run gait` would settle them.
  **HEAT IS ONE NUMBER, STARS ARE THRESHOLDS** (`COPS.star`). Writers: `heatAdd` (calls, `heatHit` from
  `dummyBlow`) and a cop's sight setting a floor of `spotV`; the only reducer is `heatStep` (cools after `lose` s
  unseen, `coolDisg`x while `!fearLooks()`). `HEAT.lx/lz` is the last reported position: a witness's own `sawX/Z`
  when his call lands, your live position while a cop sees you. `fearSees` now takes see/cone/feel so a cop's sight
  is the same LOS march as a civilian's with bigger numbers. Arrest is `playerHurt` with stun and a .25 knock --
  there is no arrest clip. Chip: `H<heat>*<stars> cs<spots>/<grabs>`. `mel.heat(n)` sets the heat.

- **FEAR IS THE OLD FLEE BRANCH WITH A NEW REASON, NOT A SECOND WAY TO RUN (m279, ROADMAP A4, `FEAR`, `fearSees`, `fearCall`).**
  `fearStep` runs in `stepDummies` before the AI and only SETS `d.fleeT` -- the same clock a blow sets in `dummyHit`
  since m38 -- so the run is `foeWander`'s own flee branch. Who can be frightened is exactly who `foeWander` drives:
  `K.ai && K.pacifist`, minus the sidekick (`pal`), the worker (`repair`), anything turned (`wasK`) and any kind whose
  file says alien/officer/clancy. Sight: distance `see`, then the cone off `d.h` (forward is `(sin h, cos h)`, so the
  bearing is `atan2(dx, dz)`) unless inside `feel`, then a line of `camHit` samples eye to eye -- the box test the
  bolts and camera use, so sight and shots agree about walls. Each body looks every `every` s, staggered by a random
  first offset. **The flee branch used `K.flee * V.pace` with no fallback** -- harmless while only kinds with a flee
  speed were ever hit, NaN for one that is merely frightened -- so it falls back to `FEAR.run`.
  `fearLooks` is the core mechanic: undisguised, or disguised as a kind whose file says alien, is an alien.
  **A speaker with an unheard `!` does not panic** (or the first quest step is impossible undisguised), and a frightened
  or calling body cannot be talked to. A caller (`callP`) stands back-to-you with a phone sprite for `callT` once the run
  ends, then `heatAdd(1, 'call')`; `HEAT` is a stub for A5. No scream recording exists, so a kind with `K.voice` grunts
  pitched up and the rest are silent. Chip: `FR<frights>/<calls> H<heat>`.

- **A QUEST STEP IS ONE QUESTION ASKED EVERY FRAME, AND IT READS THE SAVE (m278, ROADMAP A3, `QUESTS`, `questTest`).**
  Six step types -- talk / goto / reach / defeat / sample / gate -- and `questTest` is the only code that knows what
  they mean. `sample` and `gate` read `SAVE.forms` and `gate:<id>`, so they cannot pass until A6/A8 exist and need no
  edit when they do. Progress is `q:<id>` (step index) and `qdone:<id>` in `SAVE.flags`, so a reload lands on the same
  step; a `defeat` count within a step is NOT saved. `defeat` counts the EDGE into `d.st === 'down'` (`d.qDn`), because
  there is no knock-down event to listen to and a level test would count one body every frame. `talk` without `who`
  counts `talk.heard`, a counter of every finished script (TALK.said only counts first hearings) against a baseline
  taken when the step began. The beam is ONE additive cylinder, moved to `quest.tgt`; a step with nowhere to point
  hides it, and the chip says `~` after the step then. First quest is `q0 WEIRDPORT 101` (talk, knock down, get up 3 m)
  -- a stand-in until B2's Chapter 0 script. Chip: `Qq0.<step>`.

- **TALK LIVES ON THE RIGHT PAD'S TAP, AND THE LEFT TAP STAYS THE JUMP (m277, ROADMAP A2, `TALK`, `TALKS`, `talkTap`).**
  The roadmap said "the right pad lights (the existing interact pattern)" -- there was no interact pattern; the only
  lit states on `#padR` were the trigger's `arm`/`ready` (amber). So `talk` is a third class on the same `::after`
  ring in SKY, a different hue for a different meaning, and the pad's own `.hint` reads `tap = talk` / `tap = next`.
  The right tap checks `talkTap()` before the jump; m173 already put the jump on the LEFT tap too, so a body in reach
  never costs you the jump. Desktop: `E`.
  Scripts are DATA on the body (`d.talk`), seeded from `TALKS` by `mphName`, ONE speaker per kind (a street of
  hippies is one Moonbeam). Finishing one sets `talk:<id>` in the save via `progFlag` -- A3's talk step -- and that is
  why the `!` stays gone after a reload. The `!` is a Sprite PARENTED TO `d.root`, so a culled or removed body takes
  it along with no second list; its height is `drawnH` measured once, divided by the root's scale. The bubble is DOM,
  projected through the camera AFTER `stepCam` (one frame of trail otherwise) and clamped on screen.
  **NOT DONE ON PURPOSE:** the speaker does not stop or face you (his heading has one writer, his AI); nobody refuses
  an undisguised alien yet (A4 will gate `talk.near`). Chip: `T<speakers>/<heard>`, `*` while one is in reach.

- **THE SAVE IS `SAVE`, NOT `PROG` -- `PROG` IS THE BOOT CARD'S LOAD COUNTER (m276, ROADMAP A1, `SAVE`, `progSave`).**
  The roadmap asked for progress under `mel.prog`. The key is `mel.prog`; the object could not be `PROG`, because
  `const PROG = { done, total, label }` already counts GLBs for the boot card and a second `const` of that name is a
  syntax error -- a BLANK PAGE, which `npm run check` caught. So: `SAVE` holds chapter, forms (by `mphName`, `'zap'`
  always first), regions, flags, portals and juice; `progForm/Region/Portal/Flag/Chapter/Juice` are the ONLY writers and
  each saves on the spot and returns whether it changed anything, so a "quest complete" moment can fire exactly once.
  **`?fresh` DID NOT EXIST** though the roadmap said it did -- nothing in the file read it. It does now: it wipes every
  `mel.*` key in both stores (tuning, res, chip fold, world pick and the save) before anything reads them, then
  `history.replaceState`s itself out of the URL, because the world key reloads and a `?fresh` left in the bar would wipe
  the save on every tap. `mel.progReset()` is a new game that leaves the tuning alone. Chip: `CH<n>`, plus `NEW` on a
  fresh boot and `BADSAVE` when a stored save would not parse (it then starts a new game rather than throwing).

- **A BODY STANDING STILL NEVER RE-READ THE FLOOR UNDER IT (m275, `bodySeat`, `SEAT`).** *"Whenever I start the games,
  a lot of the NPCs are like through the sidewalk or the curb."* Measured before touching anything, through the real kit
  city collider (`tools/.probe/npcfloor.mjs`, his collision GLB plus the visual's lots and dirt decoded with draco):
      spawn spots                0 of 26 drawn sunk -- `kitStand` and `bodySpawn` already land on the sidewalk
      collider vs drawn ground   59 of 130,682 cells differ by 8 cm+ (curb and sidewalk edges)
      bind-pose soles            every character file at y 0 (accessor min, `lo/h` 0.000 to 0.008)
  So the spawn was never it. **Only `foeMove` (walking) and `bodyFly` (a launch) ever wrote `y`**, and `bodySep` pushes
  overlapping pairs in x and z only, so an idle body shoved onto a 25 cm sidewalk kept its road height for ever.
  `bodySeat` runs after `bodySep` every frame: every grounded body takes `groundAt(.., MOVE.step)`, the same call
  `foeMove` makes. A floor more than `SEAT.fall` below hands him to `bodyFly` as a fall, never a teleport. Leap, ride,
  the truck's rider and anything with a `vy` are skipped, because they already have a writer. Probed on the real
  collider: under the sidewalk 0 -> 0.25, off the kerb 0.25 -> 0, 2 m up -> falls, rider untouched.
  **THE CHIP SAYS WHICH CASE IT WAS.** `ST<n>` counts lifts over 5 cm. `SUNK<n>` counts bodies that still have a floor
  above their feet after the seat. **If he still sees sunk bodies with no `SUNK` in the chip, the root is right and the
  DRAWN body is low** -- a borrowed clip's Hips height (`retarget`'s `k`) or a skin offset, which nothing here can
  build to test.

- **FOUR OF HIS, ONE BUILD (m274): HER COAST IS HER IDLE, HER STRIKE RIDES, THE SWAP CLOCK RUNS ON WHEELS, THE ISLAND
  UNDERLAPS.** *"When you stop pushing she stays in the step of her stride -- we have a Rollergirl idle pose, play that when
  you're cruising... I can't melee as her... there's a ring between the island and the Weirdport border... I can't get my
  blaster out anymore when I'm the girl, and the rocket launcher as well."*
  - **COAST = `idle_normal` / `idle_backward`**, not the held stride frame (`blade_roll_*`, her r131), which froze her mid-step
    with her arms swung to one side. `BLADE.anim.rollHold` 1 puts the frame back.
  - **THE BLASTER: THE SWAP NEVER FINISHED ON WHEELS (`swapTick`).** The reach's clock was advanced inside the on-foot step
    only, so on her skates (and riding his board) `p.swap` hung part-way for ever: the weapon never arrived and `kitPick`
    refused every later pick because a swap was "still running". One function, called from both bodies. The launcher comes
    out the same way -- it was never refused, it was queued behind the hung swap.
  - **HER RIGHT FLICK IS THE STRIKE, ground and air.** `boardFlick` swallowed it (nothing on the ground, a kickflip of a deck
    she has not got in the air). On her it passes through to `meleeGo`, which she can play because she wears Zap's pool -- the
    same clips her own game borrowed.
  - **AND IT RIDES (`p.melRide`, `BLADE.melee`, her r39/r57).** On foot a strike REWRITES the velocity from its lunge, which
    on a skater is a dead stop mid-cruise. As her it keeps her velocity, adds `lunge` toward the blow and `boost` along her
    travel, and only her wheels' drag acts while it plays. **And the board re-entry took her BODY's facing as the lead** --
    which at the end of a strike is the blow, 90 deg off her line -- so 16 m/s became 2.4 on the frame the strike ended.
    Moving, the lead is her travel now. Probe: 14.2 m/s in, 14.2 lowest during, 15.4 a second and a half after.
  - **THE ISLAND'S EDGE IS MEASURED OFF THE COLLIDER, AND THE COLLIDER IS BIGGER THAN THE PICTURE.** The kit city's lots run to
    -93.5 / +93.5 on the x and z sides where the drawn ground stops at -90.3 / +90.3, so the land (2.5 m inside the collider's
    edge) began a metre outside the street and a strip of nothing showed round two sides. `ISLE.margin` 6 tucks it under
    the street everywhere. **What is still true there**: the invisible lot colliders stand 0.23 m over that strip of island,
    which is his export, not the island.

- **THE FLUNG LEG WAS MY FOOT IK SHARING SCRATCH VECTORS (m273, `bladeBody`, `_bN`/`_bN2`/`_bDV`).** *Second screenshot: standing
  still, one leg out straight at hip height, style skates already off.* Not a clip: posed through her real skeleton offline,
  no clip of hers ever lifts an ankle above 0.24 of her height. m271's `bladeBody` handed `bladeLegIK` its target offset in
  `_bV2` and the surface normal in `_bV3` -- and the IK's first lines write the KNEE's world position into `_bV2` and the
  ANKLE's into `_bV3`. So every foot was sent to ankle + knee, metres up and out, and the second foot measured its height
  against the first one's ankle. The first screenshot's "Superman" leg was probably this too, on top of the style skate.
  **THE PROBE PASSED BECAUSE IT CALLED THE IK WITH FRESH VECTORS** -- it tested the function and not the caller, which is this
  repo's oldest mistake one call deep. It now runs a stride-lifted foot END TO END through `bladeBody`: fixed, an 11 cm lift
  is set down to 1.5 cm with an 8 deg thigh correction; with the bug put back, both soles read 0.63 m in the air. **A
  module-level scratch vector may never be passed as an ARGUMENT to a function that uses the same scratch set.**

- **"STUCK IN THE SUPERMAN POSE" WAS HER STYLE SKATES, AND THEY ARE OFF (m272, `BLADE.anim.style` 0).** *"Her normal skate
  legs are super messed up, they're not even really moving and she's stuck in the Superman pose."* The screenshot is
  `blade_pose_swan_R_forward` -- arms forward, one leg straight back. m271 ported Rollergirl's r42 auto style skates:
  cruising over 5 m/s thumb-off (or over 17 pushing) she slips into one every 3 s and holds it 3.5 s, so she was in a frozen
  style pose for about half of every cruise. Those clips are the placeholders he already said he does not like (*"they were
  display holders, they're actually different skates on the ground"*) -- copying her code faithfully copied a feature he had
  rejected. Off by default, a tune row brings them back, and even then never while the thumb pushes (`styleCruise` 99).
  **THE CHIP NOW SAYS WHICH CLIP SHE IS IN** (`BLADE 14.2 push hard`, `roll`, `pose_swan_R`, `-B` for her backward set),
  because "what is she playing" cannot be read off a screenshot. Tune rows for the foot IK and the hip lean too, so if the
  legs still read wrong the two new layers can be switched off on the phone one at a time.

- **HER, COPIED RATHER THAN REBUILT (m271, `bladeAnim`, `bladeBody`, `bladeFind`, `bladeUndo`, `bladeFlipGo`,
  `bladeGunFly`, `BLADE.anim/flip/foot/hipLean/centre/gun`).** *"She's unable to be unarmed whereas by default she should
  be... it shouldn't just be locked in my hand... she has a very stiff skate... her frozen pose when she's drifting is just
  one leg out... the shooting when you're flying isn't the same... I'm looking for the same same same same."* Each of
  those had a cause, and every fix is Rollergirl's own code ported, with her numbers:
  - **UNARMED.** `stepMorph` forced the gun slot onto every disguise (m123 -- right for the DNA gun's own logic and wrong for
    her, whose game holsters by default). A blade kind now arrives on slot 0, and the left wheel takes a weapon out and puts
    it back as it does for him. The board slot is skipped while she is worn (a deck in her hands means nothing).
  - **THE STIFFNESS WAS THE GUN.** Every disguise came out holding the blaster, so every stride ran under the rifle pose with
    m265's chest steadier on top. Unarmed she skates on her whole clips; armed, `BLADE.steady` is 0 now -- her game holds
    nothing steady, it turns the body to the shot instead (below).
  - **HER MOVE BRAIN, `girlAnimMoves` LINE FOR LINE.** The push only while the thumb PUSHES along her nose (`p.thumbGo`), casual
    into hard by how hard it pushes (`p.drive`, her r84) never slower than `hardFloor`; thumb off the held roll; standing,
    `idle_normal` then a different idle every `idleHold` 7 s; cruising, a style skate every 3 s for 3.5 (her r42). Every clip
    it can play has a `__legh` half, so a gun out composes with all of them.
  - **THE "ONE LEG OUT" POSE IS HER ROLL FRAME WITHOUT HER FOOT IK.** Her game never draws that frame raw: `footGround` (r36)
    drops her until the lower skate touches and pulls a foot within 16 cm down with a two-bone IK, soles laid flat on the
    surface. Ported whole, measured on the rest pose in `mphSkin` before the mixer exists (never `skeleton.pose()` -- her r38).
    With it: her lean INTO turns at the HIPS (r27/r42) and her hips put on the turn axis (r27: the root sits 0.2 m behind
    them, which is the "boat").
  - **HER FLIPS ARE PROCEDURAL AGAIN.** Her game stopped playing flip clips at r25: a state with a clock fitted to the air
    left (`fill` .75, max 1.0 s, too little air is no flip), her held `tuck` / `flip_pose` blended on `flipShape`, and the turn
    about her HIPS, faster while tucked, landing exactly on 360. Sideways is her twist flip, not the board's barrel roll.
    Landed unfinished, the rest unwinds the short way (`settle`).
